Project: Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre Integrated Energy System
Summary/Information:
The Brimbank Aquatic and Wellness Centre Integrated Energy System project is a carbon neutral, renewable energy powered aquatic centre in western Melbourne. 
Need
Municipal aquatic centres are the highest energy consuming and greenhouse gas emitting facilities managed by councils. Heating, ventilation and cooling (HVAC) is typically the largest component of energy use at these sites, which have historically relied upon both electricity and natural gas as fuel sources.
Brimbank City Council, along with many other councils across Australia, are adopting commitments to reach net zero emissions by 2030 or sooner. Under these commitments, the use of natural gas and fossil-fuel sourced power to run council facilities is no longer tenable.
To transition away from gas, councils are looking to convert their facilities to an ‘all-electric’ equipment model, which can use greater amounts of on-site renewable energy and source any residual power needs from off-site renewable energy facilities (through power purchase agreements).
The main all-electric alternative to gas heating in aquatic centres is heat-pump technology. This technology can provide both heating and cooling. Heat pump use in cooler climates (such as Victoria and Tasmania) has been technically challenging during cooler months when the performance of air-source heat pumps decline.

Project partners: Climate-KIC Australia Limited, Sustainability Victoria, Department of Planning, Industry and Environment (NSW)

Project: Solar Power Plant Phase 1
Summary/Information: The Solar Power Plant Phase 1 project aims to develop and commercialise a utility-scale solar and storage technology in Australia.
Project partners: GHD Pty Ltd, AGL Energy Services Pty Ltd

Project: Australian Hydrogen Centre
Summary/Information: The Australian Hydrogen Centre will assess the feasibility of blending renewable hydrogen into gas distribution networks in Victoria and South Australia.
Project partners: Department for Energy and Mining, Department of Environment, Land, Water and Planning, AusNet Services, Engie Energy Services, Neoen Australia

Project: Energy Freedom Solar Electric Vehicle Pilot
Summary/Information: The Energy Freedom Solar Electric Vehicle Pilot developed by Applied Electric Vehicles Pty Ltd (AEV) will produce a lightweight, energy efficient, autonomous electric vehicle (EV) that will incorporate a solar photovoltaic (PV) roof and lithium-ion battery system.

Project: Allume Rooftop Solar Salvation Army Pilot Demonstration
Summary/Information: Allume Energy will further develop the ‘SolShare’ to enable The Salvation Army (TSA) to on-sell excess solar energy to other, separately metered tenancies in their building.
Project partners: Green Peak Energy Pty Ltd, I Want Energy Pty Ltd, Improv Pty Ltd

Project: Advancing Renewables in the Manufacturing Sector
Summary/Information: The Advancing Renewables Manufacturing Sector project will help Queensland manufacturers improve their energy productivity, reduce emissions and drive sector improvements through energy assessments, a web-based portal, knowledge sharing and public forums.
Project partners: Queensland Department of State Development, Manufacturing, Infrastructure and Planning The Australian Industry Group

Project: Rheem Active Hot Water Control
Summary/Information: The Rheem Active Hot Water Control project aims to demonstrate active control over residential hot water systems in South Australia.
Project partners: Combined Energy Technologies, Marchment Hill Consulting, SA Power Networks, Simply Energy

Project: Hornsdale Power Reserve Upgrade
Summary/Information: The Hornsdale Power Reserve Upgrade project involves a 50 MW / 64.5 MWh expansion of the Hornsdale Power Reserve, showcasing the additional benefits grid-scale batteries can provide to the National Electricity Market and Australian consumers.

Project: Frasers Property Net Zero Energy Demand Homes
Summary/Information: Frasers Property Australia will build 51 medium density energy efficient homes to demonstrate the feasibility of achieving zero energy demand homes at scale.

Project: Clean Energy Startup Support Programs
Summary/Information: The Clean Energy Startup Support Programs project will launch four programs designed to accelerate the progress of entrepreneurs deploying renewable energy and complementary technologies.
Project partners: Origin Energy Retail, Powerlink, AusNet Services, University of Technology Sydney, Clean Energy Finance Corporation

Project: Photothermal Absorption Spectrometer for Cost Reduction in PV Materials
Summary/Information: The Photothermal absorption spectrometer for cost reduction in PV materials project will accelerate solar photovoltaic (PV) research by commercialising an ultra-sensitive tool to measure contamination levels of advanced PV materials.
Arena program: Commercialisation of R&D Funding Initiative Pilot

Project: Displacement of Gas by Thermal Energy Storage
Summary/Information: The Displacement of gas by thermal energy storage project aims to demonstrate a scalable system that can displace gas use for process heating using energy from renewable resources and thermal energy storage.
Arena program: Commercialisation of R&D Funding Initiative Pilot

Project: Photoluminescence Imaging Tool
Summary/Information: The Photoluminescence Imaging Tool project will develop a prototype of a commercial photoluminescence imaging tool to monitor and diagnose the performance of solar modules located on site.
Arena program: Commercialisation of R&D Funding Initiative Pilot

Project: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) Enabler
Summary/Information: The Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) Enabler project will develop a user friendly platform that integrates product, regulation, technical, economic and construction data to create a leading Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) solution.
Arena program: Commercialisation of R&D Funding Initiative Pilot
Project partners: City of Greater Bendigo, International Energy Agency PV Power System (IEA PVPS) Task 15 BIPV, Energus, International Building Performance Simulation Association, Smart Energy Council, Australian PV Institute, Aurecon, Norman Disney & Young

Project: Pilot Project to Trial Solar F2D2
Summary/Information: The Pilot Project to Trial Solar F2D2 project aims to trial a new, advanced solar farm diagnostics and reliability enhancement tool – Solar Farm Fault Detection and Diagnosis (Solar F2D2).
Arena program: Commercialisation of R&D Funding Initiative Pilot

Project: Affordable Heating and Cooling Innovation Hub (iHub)
Summary/Information: The Affordable Heating and Cooling Innovation Hub (iHub) project aims to demonstrate how renewable energy technology can be optimally integrated with heating, ventilation, air-conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC&R) equipment in commercial buildings.
Lead organisation: The Australian Institute of Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Heating
Project partners: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, Queensland University of Technology, University of Melbourne, The University of Wollongong

Project: Mirvac Net Zero Energy Homes
Summary/Information: The Net Zero Energy Homes project will see Mirvac complete the design, marketing, sales and construction of a ‘net zero energy’ housing estate in the Melbourne suburb of Altona North.

Project: BT Imaging LIS-M1 Solar Module Inspection System
Summary/Information: This project aims to take BT Imaging’s LIS-M1 solar module inspection technology from a prototype to a large-scale trial, with prospects for commercial deployment.
Location: Alexandria, Melbourne, New South Wales, Victoria, Waterloo
Project partners: Octopus BT Imaging, Octopus Investments, 5B PV, Evolution Labs

Project: OMPS New England PHES Benefits Study
Summary/Information: The Oven Mountain Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (OMPS PHES) project will undertake a study analysing the benefits of a 600 megawatt (MW) ‘off-river’ PHES facility in the New England Renewable Energy Zone (REZ), with up to 12 hours storage.

Project: Bright Thinkers Power Station
Summary/Information: This Bright Thinkers Power Station project will develop and construct a 1.7 MW industrial rooftop solar PV system to demonstrate the Bright Thinkers Power Station (BTPS) concept.

Project: My Energy Marketplace
Summary/Information: Wattwatchers aims to build, operate and deploy the ‘My Energy Marketplace’ or MEM, a consumer-facing energy data platform, designed to securely collect, process and productise vast amounts of energy data.
Lead organisation: Energy Saving Networks Group Pty Ltd t/a Wattwatchers Digital Energy
Project partners: Australian National University (ANU), Accurassi (Knowledge-Global Pty Ltd), Cogniss (2and2 Pty Ltd), Solar Schools (iWeb Solutions Pty Ltd)

Project: APA Fortescue Solar Gas Hybrid Project
Summary/Information:
The APA Fortescue Solar Gas Hybrid Project will be developed, owned and operated by APA. The facility consists of 60 MW AC solar PV integrated with a 35 MW battery storage facility at the Newman gas-fired power station in the Pilbara region of WA.
Alinta completed the construction of the project, achieving practical completion in November 2021.
On 1 November 2023, APA Group Limited (APA) acquired Alinta’s Pilbara Energy Operations which included power generation and transmission assets in Port Hedland, Newman and included the Chichester Solar Gas Hybrid project.

Project: Capacity Improvement and Flow Balancing of CST Heating/Cooling System
Summary/Information: The project will modify Echuca Regional Health’s (ERH) existing rooftop concentrated solar thermal (CST) system to extract and utilise significantly more solar energy, more often, and to lower the cost of operating its cooling service.

Project: Feasibility Study for a Green Hydrogen and Ammonia Project
Summary/Information: The Feasibility Study for a Green Hydrogen and Ammonia Project is a study by Queensland Nitrates (QNP), Neoen and Advisian (as part of the Worley Group) of using green hydrogen to produce ammonia at QNP’s existing manufacturing plant in Queensland.
Project partners: Neoen Australia Pty Ltd, Advisian Pty Ltd (part of the Worley Group)

Project: DER Integration and Automation Project
Summary/Information: The DER Integration and Automation Project project will demonstrate how collaboration between a Distributed Energy Resources Management System (DERMS) and the GreenSync Decentralised Energy Exchange (deX) platform can unlock existing network hosting capacity to enable consumers to gain more value from their energy assets (such as solar, batteries and electric vehicles).
Project partners: GreenSync, Schneider Electric, Withywindle, SA Power Networks, Energy Queensland Limited

Project: Advancing Renewables with PCM Thermal Energy Storage
Summary/Information: The Advancing Renewables with PCM Thermal Energy Storage project aims to demonstrate the technical and economic value of thermal energy storage using phase change material (PCM) and renewable energy optimisation in commercial and industrial heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC-R).
Location: Barossa Valley, Nairne, Queensland, South Australia, Townsville
Project partners: Montague Orchards, Reef HQ Aquarium, Pernod Ricard Winemakers Pty Ltd, University of South Australia

Project: Scaling Up Environmental Upgrade Agreements Across Australia
Summary/Information: The Scaling up Environmental Upgrade Agreements Across Australia project will see the Better Building Finance program expand into NSW and SA to assist councils and businesses become more sustainable.

Project: East Rockingham Waste to Energy
Summary/Information: The East Rockingham Waste to Energy project will process up to 330,000 tonnes of residual waste per annum and recover energy to produce 28.9 MW of power.
Lead organisation: Tribe Infrastructure, New Energy Corporation, HZI

Project: Powerlink Cost-Effective System Strength Study
Summary/Information: The Powerlink Cost-Effective System Strength Study will promote increased awareness of system strength and measures that can be used to manage it, including centralised and coordinated solutions.
Project partners: Sun Metals Corporation, Pacific Hydro, GHD

Project: Logan City Biosolids Gasification Project
Summary/Information: The Logan City Biosolids Gasification Project is an Australian first initiative that demonstrates how sewage sludge can be transformed into energy.
Project partners: Downer Utilities, WSP Australia, Cardno (QLD), Pyrocal

Project: Battery of the Nation Future State NEM Analysis (Stage 2)
Summary/Information: Hydro Tasmania’s Stage 2 analysis of the future energy market provides perspective on the technical and economic models and frameworks that underpin the Battery of the Nation opportunity.

Project: Renewable Green Hydrogen Feasibility
Summary/Information: The Feasibility of Renewable Green Hydrogen project will conduct and assess the feasibility of producing renewable green hydrogen and ammonia at Dyno Nobel’s existing facility in Moranbah, Queensland.

Project: Agnew Renewable Energy Microgrid
Summary/Information: A Western Australian gold mine will be the first Australian mine to be powered by a wind, solar, battery and gas microgrid.
Lead organisation: Agnew Gold Mining Company Pty Ltd
Project partners: Energy Developments Limited, Goldwind, Juwi, Cummins

Project: Solar PV Module Design
Summary/Information: The Solar PV Module Design project aims to design a solar PV module that lowers operating temperatures, increases power output and improves a system’s lifespan to further increase solar’s competitiveness.
Lead organisation: The University of New South Wales

Project: Module Design for Lower Field Operating Temperature & Improved Yield Study
Summary/Information: This project aims to design a solar PV module that lowers operating temperatures, increases power output and improves a system’s lifespan to further increase solar’s competitiveness.
Lead organisation: The University of New South Wales

Project: United Energy Voltage Controlled Frequency Regulation System
Summary/Information: The United Energy Voltage Controlled Frequency Regulation System will test United Energy’s Dynamic Voltage Management System capability to deliver Frequency Control Ancillary Services (FCAS) to the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) and the National Electricity Market (NEM)

Project: National Ultrafast EV Charging Infrastructure Network
Summary/Information: The National Ultrafast EV Charging Infrastructure Network project by Evie Networks will be deploying Australia’s largest ultra-fast charging infrastructure network. This project will play a significant role in improving Australia’s electric vehicle (EV) readiness by removing driver range anxiety, which is one of the major barriers that limits the adoption of EVs.
Lead organisation: Fast Cities Australia Pty Ltd (trading as Evie Networks)

Project: National Energy Simulator Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO), in collaboration with the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), is undertaking the National Energy Simulator Feasibility Study to develop a first-in-class, cross-domain, and highly detailed simulation system of Australia’s energy systems.
Project partners: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO)

Project: Renewable Hydrogen Production and Refuelling Project
Summary/Information: The Renewable Hydrogen Production and Refuelling Project aims to demonstrate renewable hydrogen production at a commercially viable scale, and help progress the commercialisation of hydrogen for vehicle transport in Australia.
Project partners: ITM Power, Queensland University of Technology, Hyundai Motor Company Australia

Project: Commercialisation of Renewable Crude Oil Production
Summary/Information: Southern Oil Refining Pty Ltd aims to build and operate a demonstration scale hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) reactor to produce crude oil from biosolids (a by-product of treated wastewater) that will be capable of scaling up to commercial scale. The renewable crude oil will be upgraded to renewable diesel (and potentially jet fuel) using the existing facilities at the Northern Oil Refining facility in Gladstone, Queensland.
Project partners: Melbourne Water Corporation, Queensland Urban Utilities

Project: AEMO Virtual Power Plant Demonstrations
Summary/Information: A Virtual Power Plant (VPP) broadly refers to a group of resources that are coordinated using software and communications technology to deliver services traditionally performed by a conventional power plant. In Australia, grid-connected VPPs focus on coordinating rooftop photovoltaic (PV), battery storage and controllable load devices.

Project: Decentralised Energy Exchange (deX) Program
Summary/Information: GreenSync’s Decentralised Energy Exchange (deX) is a market-enabling digital platform that aims to provide electricity networks with better coordination and control of the increasing volume of distributed energy resources (DER) in the electricity grid. deX also aims to enable consumers to get more value from their energy assets (such as solar, batteries and electric vehicles), by being rewarded for participating in grid services.

Project: UniWave200 King Island Project - Wave Swell
Summary/Information: The UniWave200 King Island Project included the design, construction, deployment, installation and operation of the UniWave200, a 200KW wave energy converter near Grassy Harbour on King Island, Tasmania.

Project: Intermittent Dynamic Electrowinning Using Renewable Energy
Summary/Information: Element 25’s (E25) Pilot studies for Intermittent Dynamic Electrowinning (IDE) Using Renewable Energy Project will examine the viability of using renewable energy to power E25’s Butcherbird metal production process in Western Australia.

Project: Lake Bonney Stages 2/3
Summary/Information: This Lake Bonney Stages 2/3 project introduces a short-term wind production forecasting product into the Australian market from Vestas, Australia’s largest wind energy solution provider, and its wholly owned subsidiary Utopus Insights, an energy analytics provider with 15 years of experience in energy software solutions.
Lead organisation: Vestas - Australian Wind Technology Pty Ltd
Project partners: Infigen Energy Services Pty Limited, Utopus Insights, Inc.\

Project: Solar Power Ensemble Forecaster
Summary/Information: Accurately forecasting the output of grid connected solar systems is critical to increasing the overall penetration of solar and renewables on the electrical network. This is important for the stability and management of the electrical system as a whole.
Project partners: University of South Australia Centre for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, University of New South Wales, CSIRO

Project: Ararat Wind Farm
Summary/Information: Forecasts for wind generators operating in the National Electricity Market (NEM) have historically been provided by the Australian Wind Energy Forecasting System (AWEFS).

Project: Using Upstream LIDAR Measurements
Summary/Information: In this Using Upstream LIDAR Measurements project, Windlab will use upstream LIDAR wind profile measurements to augment (supervisory control and data acquisition) SCADA information currently provided to the machine learning algorithms used in 5-minute-ahead wind forecasts.

Project: Charge Together Phase 2
Summary/Information: Evenergi’s Charge Together – Phase 2 project will develop an online platform to help businesses and consumers make informed choices about electric vehicles (EVs), and assist electricity networks to plan for the potential impact of EVs.
Project partners: Ausgrid, NSW Government, NRMA and South Australian Government

Project: Lastek Measurement Guidelines for Tandem Solar Cells Project
Summary/Information: The Lastek Measurement Guidelines for Tandem Solar Cells Project develops equipment and procedures to accurately measure the performance of multi-junction (tandem) solar cells. It creates new Australian capability to support growth in tandem solar cell research, which is expected to underpin the next wave of performance improvements for solar PV.

Project: Toyota Ecopark Hydrogen Demonstration
Summary/Information:
The Toyota Ecopark Hydrogen Demonstration project transformed part of Toyota Australia’s decommissioned car manufacturing plant in Altona (VIC) into a renewable energy hub to produce renewable hydrogen for both stationary energy and transport energy uses.
The project demonstrated the technical and economic feasibility of producing, storing, and using hydrogen sourced from renewable powered electrolysis.

Project: REALM: Renewable Energy and Load Management
Summary/Information: REALM is a feasibility study which demonstrates how optimally integrating on-site renewables, storage and energy productivity can reduce business costs and emissions, while simultaneously supporting the network.
Location: New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Victoria
Project partners: Australian Alliance for Energy Productivity, Schneider Electric

Project: Wind Forecasting for the NEM
Summary/Information: Fulcrum3D’s wind forecasting for the NEM project aims to reduce uncertainty in wind power generation by providing the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) with high accuracy, short-term wind power forecasts. The project will utilise a turbine agnostic wind forecasting model with distributed sensors.
Location: New South Wales, South Australia, Victoria

Project: evolve DER Project
Summary/Information: The evolve DER project aims to increase the network hosting capacity of distributed energy resources (DER) by maximising their participation in energy, ancillary and network service markets, while ensuring the secure technical limits of the electricity networks are not breached.
Location: Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, Queensland
Project partners: The ANU, Energy Queensland, Ergon Energy, Energex, Essential Energy, Endeavour Energy, Ausgrid, Reposit Power, Evergen, Redback Technologies, SwitchDIn, NSW Government

Project: Aeolius Wind Forecasting Project
Summary/Information: The Aeolius Wind Forecasting Project led by Aeolius Wind Systems Pty Ltd aims to demonstrate two innovative and complementary energy forecasting technologies for use in the National Electricity Market (NEM).
Project partners: AGL Energy Ltd, Curtin University, Adelaide University

Project: Proa Analytics Solar Forecasts
Summary/Information: The Innovative Optimally Combined Solar Forecasts project recognises that power output of a solar farm fluctuates due to cloud motion over the site.
Project partners: Sieltec Canarias, Oakey 1 Asset Company Pty Ltd, Genex Power Limited

Project: Wind Forecasting Demonstration Project
Summary/Information: Meridian Energy Australia (MEA) and the University of Melbourne are developing innovative techniques to improve 5 minute ahead, Unconstrained Intermittent Generation Forecasts (UIGF) for the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO).

Project: Advanced VPP Grid Integration
Summary/Information: The Advanced VPP Grid Integration project aims to show how higher levels of energy exports to the grid from customer solar and battery systems can be enabled through dynamic, rather than fixed, export limits, and to test the value this can create for customers and Virtual Power Plant (VPP) operators.

Project: Enhanced Reliability Through Short Time Resolution Data
Summary/Information: Increased penetration of distributed energy resources (DER) are leaving power system operations vulnerable to the operating behaviour of a multitude of diverse, distributed generators.

Project: Smart Hot Water System
Summary/Information: The Smart Hot Water System project aims to prove that a fleet of systems can be centrally controlled to manage reverse power flows into the grid and improve power system reliability.
Project partners: Reposit Power, WheezyTech, Wilson Industries, Citipower, Powercor Australia, United Energy Distribution

Project: Community Models for Deploying and Operating DER
Summary/Information: The increasing prevalence of behind­-the­-meter solar generation and battery storage is often motivated by high network tariffs, which discourage the transport of energy between generation, storage and load assets that are not co-­located.
Location: Australian Capital Territory, Queensland, Tasmania, Victoria
Project partners: Energy Consumers Australia, Energy Networks Association, Enova Community Energy, RePower, Shoalhaven, TasNetworks, Thinking In Colours, Totally Renewable Yackandandah, Evoenergy

Project: Solar Farm Solutions & the Australian Energy Sector
Summary/Information: The Solar Farm Solutions & the Australian Energy Sector project aims to operationalise, deploy and improve self-forecasting technology for up to eight Australian solar farms and to submit dispatch forecasts to the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) to reduce costs to large-scale solar farms.
Lead organisation: Solar and Storage Modelling Pty Ltd
Location: New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Victoria
Project partners: Wirsol, Oakey 1 Asset Company Pty Ltd, Neoen Australia, Foresight Group, First Solar, EnergyAustralia, Edify Energy, FRV, Dispatch Solutions, CWP Renewables

Project: Optimal DER Scheduling for Frequency Stability
Summary/Information: This Optimal DER Scheduling for Frequency Stability study will investigate how to optimally schedule distributed energy resources (DER) to provide low-cost frequency stability services within distribution network constraints and while respecting the motivations and primary functionality desired by DER owners (i.e. reduced cost, independence etc.)
Project partners: The ANU, TasNetworks, Powerlink Queensland, Technische Universitat Berlin

Project: Advanced Planning of PV-Rich Distribution Networks Study
Summary/Information: This project will develop analytical techniques to assess residential solar PV hosting capacity of electricity distribution networks by leveraging existing network and customer data. This project will also produce planning recommendations to increase solar PV hosting capacity using non-traditional solutions that exploit the capabilities of PV inverters, voltage regulation devices, and battery energy storage systems.

Project: Hydrostor Angas A-CAES Project
Summary/Information: The Hydrostor Angas A-CAES Project is Australia’s first Advanced Compressed Air Energy Storage (A-CAES) facility.

Project: Advanced Energy Resources Wind, Solar and Battery Project
Summary/Information: Second-hand wind turbines, solar and a battery will combine to power a remote mine in Western Australia.

Project: Demonstration of Three Dynamic Grid-Side Technologies
Summary/Information: The Demonstration of Three Dynamic Grid-Side Technologies project aims to roll out three novel technologies and intelligent control systems to understand and demonstrate their ability to increase the uptake of distributed energy resources (DER) at the neighbourhood level, safely and cost-effectively.
Project partners: AusNet Services, University of NSW, State Grid International Development Co.

Project: Distributed Energy Resources Hosting Capacity Study
Summary/Information: The project aims to demonstrate the issues faced by Australian distribution networks in maintaining security and quality of supply in the context of increasing distributed energy resource (DER) penetration.

Project: Conversion of Remote Crude Oil Beam Pumps to Solar & Battery
Summary/Information: Santos’ trial project will convert 56 crude oil beam pumps, which are engine powered to 100 per cent renewable solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery storage systems.

Project: National Low-Voltage Feeder Taxonomy Study
Summary/Information: The National Low-Voltage Feeder Taxonomy Study aims to produce the first national low-voltage network taxonomy that outlines the real-world characteristics of the distribution system.
Project partners: Energy Networks Australia, Ausgrid, AusNet Electricity Services, Western Power, Endeavour Energy, Energy Queensland, Essential Energy, Horizon Power, SA Power Networks, TasNetworks

Project: Dynamic Limits DER Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Dynamic Limits DER Feasibility Study will explore implementing dynamic distributed energy resources (DER) export limits to better manage voltage and thermal constraints on the electricity network.

Project: Gullen Range Wind Farm Field Study
Summary/Information: Goldwind successfully installed and tested the Inertia-Based Fast Frequency Response (IBFFR) on 10 wind turbines at Gullen Range Wind Farm in NSW, supported by the wind farm’s owner BJCE Australia.

Project: Pricing and Integration of Distributed Energy Resources
Summary/Information: The project examines a way to value & provide pricing and integration for distributed energy resources services within network and customer sites. This includes direct customer DER, aggregation of DER, wholesale market integration of DER, and the use of DER for ancillary services and reserves.
Project partners: Australian Energy Council Limited, Australian Energy Market Operation Limited, Energy Consumers Australia Limited, Total Environment Centre Inc, Enel X (formally EnerNOC), OC Energy, GreenSync

Project: Indra Monash Smart City
Summary/Information: The Indra Monash Smart City will demonstrate how smart and renewable technologies can be integrated at the Monash University Clayton embedded network to maintain power quality and test market driven responses and business models.

Project: Residential Heat Pump Study
Summary/Information: The Residential Heat Pump Study is a three-year study on the commercial-scale demonstration of renewable (thermal energy) ground source heat pumps (GSHPs). Based in the Fairwater master-planned residential community in Western Sydney, the project seeks to establish the business case for industry-wide adoption of using GSHPs to provide residential heating and cooling in greenfield developments.
Project partners: Presync, Frasers, New South Wales Office of Environment and Heritage, University of Technology Sydney, Curtin University, Wattwatchers, Green Building Council of Australia

Project: Accelerating the Growth Development of Energy Monitoring
Summary/Information: This project will deploy technologies to accelerate the growth of energy monitoring for households and small businesses with rooftop solar.

Project: Application of Advanced Short Term Power Generation Forecasting
Summary/Information: Sustainably integrating wind and solar power into the national electricity grid requires precise forecasting of power output from wind and solar farms.
Project partners: Monash University, Palisade Investment Partners Limited

Project: Mount Piper Energy Recovery Project Final Investment Decision Study
Summary/Information: The Mount Piper Energy Recovery Project Final Investment Decision Study is a technical and economic feasibility study of converting waste to energy and providing steam for integration into Mount Piper Power Station in NSW.

Project: Chargefox Electric Vehicle Charging Network Project
Summary/Information: The Chargefox Electric Vehicle Charging Network Project will play a significant part in improving Australia’s infrastructure and remove one of the major barriers that limits the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs).
Location: New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Victoria, Western Australia

Project: Kwinana Energy Recovery Project
Summary/Information: Kwinana Energy Recovery will be the first facility in Australia that integrates recovery and reuse of waste with the generation of electricity set to deliver renewable baseload power to a large metropolitan population and an industrial base. The facility will use world-class technologies to process 460,000 tonnes per year of residual non-recyclable waste. Kwinana Energy Recovery will not only process non-recyclable waste for energy recovery, but it will also produce ash by-products which are used internationally for construction materials such as bricks and aggregate for roads.
Project partners: Acciona, Veolia, Keppel SeghersEnd Date reflects the completion of the ARENA Funding Agreement when all obligations are met, not the date of construction completion

Project: Ausgrid Power2U Project
Summary/Information: The Ausgrid Power2U project involves the establishment a $4.1 million fund to help selected customers to permanently reduce their electricity use on Ausgrid’s network. By permanently reducing customer demand for grid supplied electricity, Ausgrid can delay, or avoid, network investment and, over time, lower the cost of electricity for all customers.

Project: Fulcrum3D CloudCAM Solar Forecasting
Summary/Information: The Fulcrum3D CloudCAM solar forecasting project aims to provide high accuracy short-term power forecasts utilising all-sky cameras and state-of-the-art software. The project will forecast power generated at Genex Power’s 50 MW Kidston Solar Farm in Queensland (including reduction in output from cloud cover) to reduce uncertainty in solar power generation.

Project: Business Renewables Centre Australia
Summary/Information: The Business Renewables Centre Australia project will establish the first Business Renewables Centre in Australia (BRC-A) – an online resource centre and marketplace platform, supported by face-to-face events and training to increase renewable energy use within Australian organisations (particularly commercial and industrial energy users).

Project: Project Marinus: Further Bass Strait Interconnection
Summary/Information: The Project Marinus project led by TasNetworks will receive up to $10 million of funding from ARENA to further investigate how the Bass Strait interconnection might form a key part of Australia’s future electricity and telecommunications grid.

Project: Shoalhaven Pumped Hydro Expansion Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Shoalhaven Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (PHES) feasibility study will explore the technical and commercial feasibility of expanding the existing Shoalhaven PHES Scheme.

Project: Cities Power Partnership
Summary/Information: The Cities Power Partnership (CPP) is the largest local government climate program, with 100 councils representing almost 11 million Australians.

Project: BMS-Inverter Hybrid Project
Summary/Information: The BMS-Inverter Hybrid Project combines two central components in battery storage systems – the battery management system and the inverter – into a single solution, leading to lower system costs and increased lifespan.

Project: Jemena Power to Gas Demonstration
Summary/Information: The Jemena Power to Gas Demonstration project involves designing and constructing a Power-to-Gas (P2G) facility which will source renewable electricity and convert it into hydrogen via electrolysis.

Project: Middleback Ranges PHES Pre-Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Middleback Ranges PHES Pre-Feasibility Study is a study for the development of a PHES plant at a mine site known as the “Iron Duchess North” in the Middleback Ranges, South Australia. The base case for the pre-feasibility study is 110MW dispatchable power and six hours storage with consideration to increase capacity to 220MW.

Project: Bio Inspired Hydrogen Generation
Summary/Information: Electrolysis uses Electrical Energy to convert Water into the Clean Fuel, Hydrogen, with pure Oxygen as a bi-product. This Bio Inspired Hydrogen Generation project, using inspiration from Nature, will develop a new Electrolysis Technology, more simple and efficient than any known to operate from pure water and renewably generated electricity.
Location: Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales

Project: Improving Efficiency, Durability & Cost-effectiveness of III-V Semiconductors
Summary/Information: This project aims to demonstrate a photo electrochemical system using III-V multi-junction semiconductors through cost-effective epitaxial lift-off techniques that are surface modified for robust operation.
Project partners: MicroLink Devices, Inc., University of Michigan

Project: Efficient Solar Hydrogen Generation
Summary/Information: The Efficient Solar Hydrogen Generation project investigates the fabrication and integration of low-cost semiconductors and earth abundant catalysts to address one of the most significant challenges for hydrogen production: the development of efficient, stable and cheap solar water splitting systems.
Project partners: Shenzhen Kohodo Hydrogen Energy, University of New South Wales

Project: CSIRO - Solar Thermochemical Hydrogen Research and Development
Summary/Information: The Solar Thermochemical Hydrogen Research and Development project will demonstrate Australia’s first solar thermal beam down system, concentrating solar energy from a heliostat field in order to heat a fluidised bed on the ground to 1300 °C.
Project partners: Niigata University, Japan Institute of Applied Energy (IAE)

Project: Hydrogen to Ammonia Research and Development
Summary/Information: The Hydrogen to Ammonia Research and Development project is to develop an ammonia production process which is less energy intensive than the conventional Haber-Bosch process and does not contribute to any greenhouse gas emissions.
Project partners: Orica Australia Pty, Grains Research and Development Corporation

Project: Methane Fuel Carrier Research and Development
Summary/Information: The Methane Fuel Carrier Research and Development project will investigate the production of synthetic methane as a readily exportable, renewable fuel, derived from atmospheric carbon dioxide and hydrogen produced from renewable sources.

Project: Liquid Fuel Carrier Research and Development
Summary/Information: The Liquid Fuel Carrier Research and Development project proposes a game changing technology for conversion of solar energy to liquid fuels.
Project partners: Johnson Matthey, BG Negev Technologies and Applications

Project: Biological Hydrogen Production
Summary/Information: The Biological Hydrogen Production project will produce a bacteria that can efficiently and rapidly convert sugars from various renewable sources into hydrogen gas.

Project: Low-Cost, Robust, High-Activity Water Splitting Electrodes
Summary/Information: The Water Splitting Electrodes project will develop scalable methods for the fabrication of efficient, low-cost and robust electrodes for Hydrogen production from renewable energy sources via electrochemical water splitting.
Lead organisation: Monash Energy Materials and System Institute (MEMSI)

Project: Ammonia Production from Renewables
Summary/Information: The project will develop high-performing electrodes for direct electrochemical conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia – a readily exportable carrier of renewable energy.

Project: QUT Hydrogen Process Research & Development
Summary/Information: The QUT Hydrogen Process Research & Development project develops a scalable and systematic process to evaluate the viability of decentralised and regional-scale renewable energy hybrid systems to generate hydrogen from sustainable resources.
Project partners: Swinburne University of Technology, Sumitomo Electric Industries, Griffith University, Energy Developments Limited, CS Energy

Project: Proton Flow Reactor System
Summary/Information: The Proton Flow Reactor System project aims to develop an integrated system for storage of electricity from renewable energy and export the stored energy as hydrogen within hydrogenated carbon-based material.
Project partners: Eldor Corporation, Institute for Carbon-Neutral Energy Research, Kyushu University

Project: Enabling Efficient, Affordable & Robust Use of Renewable Hydrogen
Summary/Information: This project will demonstrate the performance and the value of highly efficient, reciprocating engines operating on renewable hydrogen. These engines are intended to be the most efficient, hydrogen fuelled engines ever developed, with supporting research enabling this goal. We will then analyse how these engines are an important part of different, economically optimal, integrated systems that generate, transport or use renewable hydrogen.
Project partners: University of New South Wales, MAN Diesel & Turbo SE, Energy Power Systems Australia Pty Ltd, Continental Automotive Systems Inc, Energy Australia

Project: Highly Efficient & Low Cost Photovoltaic-Electrolysis System
Summary/Information: The Highly Efficient & Low Cost Photovoltaic-Electrolysis System project is a promising approach to produce renewable hydrogen (H2) for export from sunlight and water. The main obstacle to utilising PVE to produce H2 is the high cost and modest efficiency.
Project partners: Beijing Zhongchao Haiqi Technology, RayGen Resources, Shenzhen Kohodo Sunshine Renewable Energy Co.

Project: Waste Biomass to Renewable Hydrogen
Summary/Information: Extracting hydrogen from biomass represents a valuable approach by which a waste organic stream can be converted into hydrogen (or hydrogen-carriers) for downstream use or as an exportable commodity.
Project partners: Beijing Origin Water Technology, Apricus Energy

Project: UWA Methanol from Syngas Research & Development
Summary/Information: Methanol is an excellent hydrogen carrier. It can be easily manufactured from renewable resources, easily transported and stored in liquid form, and can be readily converted to hydrogen at the point of use or used directly as a clean and low-carbon transport fuel.

Project: Lake Bonney Battery Energy Storage System
Summary/Information: The Lake Bonney Battery Energy Storage System project involves the installation, testing and commercial operation of a 25MW / 52MWh Tesla battery energy storage system that will be co-located with the existing 278.5MW Lake Bonney wind farm in South Australia.

Project: SolPod Solar PV Demonstration Project
Summary/Information: Solpods are innovative solar racking systems designed for large flat roofs, typical of commercial or industrial buildings. The project aims to increase the uptake of solar PV in the commercial and industrial sectors by offering commercial tenants a cost-competitive solar system that is able to be redeployed elsewhere.

Project: Ethtec Cellulosic Ethanol Pilot Plant
Summary/Information: The Ethtec Cellulosic Ethanol Pilot Plant project will demonstrate Ethtec’s innovative and cost-effective approach to the production of cellulosic ethanol and other renewable chemicals through the construction of a Pilot Plant.

Project: Enerverter Project Aztec
Summary/Information: The Enerverter Project Aztec project by Restech is a small, packaged power inverter that can manage and control simultaneous power sources (including AC mains, battery power and solar PV) to operate industrial sized motors directly from PV with grid back up.

Project: Battery Storage System Performance Standard
Summary/Information: Currently, it is difficult to fairly compare the performance of commercially available battery storage equipment (BSE) on the market, as there is no common standard for how performance characteristics are to be measured and reported.
Project partners: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), Smart Energy Council, Deakin University, The State of Victoria as represented by the Department of Environment, Land, Water and Planning

Project: Repurposing the Tarraleah Hydropower Scheme
Summary/Information: The Repurposing the Tarraleah Hydropower Scheme project is a $5 million feasibility study on repurposing the Tarraleah hydropower scheme to produce more energy, more flexibly in the future, based on a preferred capacity option identified in the pre-feasibility study.

Project: Hardwood Residue Bio-Refinery Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Hardwood Residue Bio-Refinery Feasibility Study explored the viability of converting hardwood sawmill residue into higher value energy products.

Project: Technology Collaboration Program for Demand Side Management
Summary/Information: A study of enabling technologies to enhance Australian participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Program (TCP) for Demand Side Management.

Project: NSW Schools Energy Productivity Program (SEPP) Pilot
Summary/Information: The NSW Schools Energy Productivity (SEPP) program ran from April 2018 – June 2019 and demonstrated the benefits of integrating energy productivity improvements and renewable energy across NSW schools. The aim was to accelerate widespread adoption in schools and leave a legacy of increased skills, capacity and knowledge to extend beyond the pilot.

Project: Bioenergy Australia Participation in the IEA TCP on Bioenergy
Summary/Information: Bioenergy Australia will represent Australia on the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP) on Bioenergy.

Project: Cultana Pumped Hydro Energy Storage Phase 2
Summary/Information: EnergyAustralia and Arup are proposing the development of a 225 MW pumped hydro energy storage project using seawater near Port Augusta, South Australia.

Project: Ocean Energy Systems Technology Collaboration Program
Summary/Information: CSIRO will lead Australia’s participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) – Ocean Energy Systems (OES) programme to strengthen Australia’s voice, influence and knowledge in ocean energy developments and research.
Project partners: Climate-KIC, University of Adelaide, Swinburne University of Technology, UNSW, University of Tasmania, University of Western Australia

Project: BioDICE Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The project will investigate the feasibility of dispatchable, cost-effective power from forest and mill wastes using adapted diesel engines (direct injection carbon engine – bioDICE).

Project: Solar Power and Chemical Energy Systems
Summary/Information: A study of solar thermal technologies to enhance Australian participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Program (TCP) for Solar Power and Chemical Energy Systems (SolarPACES).

Project: Missions Innovation Challenge - Affordable Heating and Cooling
Summary/Information: This project supported Australian participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Mission Innovation Challenge for Affordable Heating and Cooling of Buildings.

Project: Smart Grids Innovation Challenge
Summary/Information: CSIRO will lead Australia’s participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Mission Innovation Challenge for Smart Grids.

Project: Converting Sunlight Innovation Challenge
Summary/Information: This project supports Australian participation in the Mission Innovation Converting Sunlight Innovation Challenge.
Project partners: ANU, Curtin University, Flinders University, QUT, University of Melbourne, UNSW, Arizona State University, DLR, Niigata University, Sandia National Laboratories

Project: International Energy Agency Hydropower Technology Collaboration Program
Summary/Information: This project supports Australian participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Program (TCP) for hydropower.
Project partners: Charles Sturt University, Kator Research Services, Entura

Project: Mission Innovation Challenge ' Off-Grid Access to Electricity
Summary/Information: This project aims to improve sustainable electricity access planning for off-grid households and communities in Pacific Island countries.
Lead organisation: The University of New South Wales

Project: IEA Technology Collaboration Programme PV Power Systems
Summary/Information: This project supports Australian representation on the International Energy Agency (IEA) PV Power Systems (PVPS) Technology Collaboration Programme. It aims to increase the use of solar PV by delivering quality research, data and information and by coordinating Australia’s engagement in the initiative.
Project partners: University of New South Wales, Ekistica, Sunwiz

Project: IEA Technology Collaboration Programme - Solar Heating and Cooling
Summary/Information: This project supports Australian representation on the International Energy Agency (IEA) Solar Heating and Cooling (SHC) Technology Collaboration Programme. It aims to promote the use of all aspects of solar thermal energy and coordinate Australia’s engagement in the initiative.
Project partners: University of New South Wales, Sustainable Energy Transformation

Project: Promoting Hydrogen Implementation and Utilization
Summary/Information: A study of hydrogen technologies to enhance Australian participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Program (TCP) for Hydrogen.

Project: ATCO Hydrogen Microgrid
Summary/Information: ATCO believes Australia’s gas distribution network will play a key role in the future energy mix, bringing natural gas and new ‘clean’ gas, including hydrogen, to customers playing a central role in reducing energy costs and carbon emissions and an ideal complement to intermittent renewable energy like wind and solar.

Project: Open Source Grid Integration Model for the National Electricity Market
Summary/Information: The Open Source Grid Integration Model for the National Electricity Market project will develop a detailed web-based open source grid integration and optimisation Modelling Tool for the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM).
Project partners: United States Strategic Energy Analysis Center of the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, The Centre for Energy and Environmental Markets, University of New South Wales, Energy Transitions Hub, University of Melbourne, ThoughtWorks Australia Pty Ltd, New South Wales State Government, Victorian State Government, South Australian State Government

Project: Promoting Hydrogen Implementation and Utilization in Australia
Summary/Information: This project supports Australian participation in the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Program (TCP) on hydrogen over five years (2018 to 2023).
Location: New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, Western Australia

Project: SOURCE Hydropanel Demonstration Project
Summary/Information: The SOURCE Hydropanel Demonstration Project supports the pilot demonstration of 150 SOURCE Hydropanels in Australia.

Project: Latrobe Valley Microgrid Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Latrobe Valley Microgrid Feasibility Study will assess the viability of creating a local energy marketplace for dairy farms, residential participants and commercial/industrial customers in the Latrobe Valley.

Project: Tasmanian Pumped Hydro Energy Storage Opportunities Stage 2
Summary/Information: The Tasmanian Pumped-Hydro Energy Storage Opportunities Stage 2 project will conduct pre-feasibility studies on 14 proposed pumped hydro energy storage (PHES) sites under the Hydro Tasmania-led Battery of the Nation Program.

Project: Simply Energy Virtual Power Plant (VPP)
Summary/Information: The Simply Energy Virtual Power Plant (VPP) project will deliver up to 1200 Tesla Powerwall 2 batteries to Adelaide households.

Project: SA Strategic Regional Electric Vehicle Adoption Program
Summary/Information: The SA Strategic Regional Electric Vehicle Adoption Program project goal is to accelerate EV adoption, help to optimise infrastructure investment and help ensure that EVs are powered by renewable energy.
Project partners: SA Power Networks, Adelaide Council, South Australian Government, Australian Electric Vehicle Association

Project: Solar Rooftop Electricity Retailer
Summary/Information: A demonstration of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies through establishing Australia’s first customer-owned rooftop solar PV focussed electricity retailer and solar service company, in doing so supporting the transition to the distributed energy future.

Project: MSM Milling Biomass Fuel Switch Project
Summary/Information: The MSM Milling Biomass Fuel Switch project involves replacing current LPG fuelled boilers with a 5 MW biomass fuelled boiler using locally sourced timber residue as a fuel source.

Project: Musselroe Wind Farm FCAS Trial
Summary/Information: The Musselroe Wind Farm FCAS Trial project is aimed at understanding the economic and commercial case for FCAS participation by wind farms and if viable, enabling the frequency controllers at Musselroe Wind Farm.
Lead organisation: Musselroe Wind Farm Pty Ltd (Woolnorth Wind Farm Holding Pty Ltd)

Project: Ballarat Energy Storage System (BESS)
Summary/Information: $25 million will be provided to a consortia led by Spotless Sustainability Services to build Ballarat Energy Storage System (BESS) – a 30 megawatt (MW) / 30 megawatt-hour (MWh) large-scale, grid-connected battery located at the Ballarat electricity station (Ballarat Area Terminal Station (BATS).

Project: Gannawarra Energy Storage System (GESS)
Summary/Information: The Gannawarra Energy Storage System (GESS) is a 25 megawatt (MW)/50 megawatt-hour (MWh) lithium-ion battery to be co-located with the 60 MW(DC) Gannawarra Solar Farm located west of Kerang in north western Victoria.

Project: Social Access Solar Gardens
Summary/Information: The Social Access Solar Gardens Project will prototype four of the first solar gardens projects in Australia in locations across New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria. The Project aims to enable solar gardens that will benefit the 30% of Australian consumers currently excluded from owning solar PV.
Project partners: NSW Government, Bendigo Sustainability Group, Blacktown Council, Brotherhood of St Laurence, Byron Shire Council, Community Owned Renewable Energy Mullumbimbi (COREM), Community Power Agency, Energy Queensland, Enova Community, Energy Institute for Sustainable Futures, University of Technology Sydney, Norton Rose Fullbright, Pingala, Powershop, Queensland Council of Social Services, Repower Shoalhaven, Shoalhaven Council, Swan Hill Shire Council

Project: Next Generation Silicon Sub-Cells
Summary/Information:
This Next Generation Silicon Sub-Cells project saw UNSW work with partners at the Ohio State University to develop high efficiency III-V on silicon multi-junction solar cells suitable for commercial development.
Melding UNSWs leading silicon solar cell expertise with the latest developments in combining III-V materials with silicon a new generation of solar cells was realised. At its conclusion the project delivered key insights into the design and fabrication of high efficiency silicon sub-cells, as well as commercially viable processes for manufacturing silicon based high efficiency multi-junction solar cells in the short term and more novel designs in the longer term.

Project: Monash University Building Integrated PV Study
Summary/Information: The Monash University Building Integrated PV Study project will focus on the development of high efficiency, semi-transparent perovskite photovoltaics (PV) for use as building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) windows.
Project partners: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), CSR Viridian, GreatCell Solar Industries

Project: Metallised Encapsulant for Silicon PV Modules
Summary/Information: The Metallised Encapsulant for Silicon PV Modules project will develop an innovative module fabrication technology where conductors are directly electroformed in laser-structured encapsulant surfaces.

Project: Advanced High-Efficiency Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: In this Advanced High-Efficiency Silicon Solar Cells project, we exploit the unique capabilities of Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) to synthesise innovative surface and contact passivating stacks.

Project: Hydrogenated and Hybrid Heterojunction P-Type Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The University of New South Wales has received a funding grant from ARENA to conduct research on the development of high-efficiency, low-cost p-type solar cells silicon solar cells in conjunction with the Australian National University and Arizona State University.

Project: Development of Novel Hydrogen Trapping Techniques
Summary/Information: UNSW Sydney has received a funding grant from ARENA to develop new recently patented techniques for trapping and controlling hydrogen within highly defective silicon to enable higher solar cell efficiencies while using cheaper silicon wafer sources.

Project: Hydrogenated Bifacial PERL Silicon PV Cells
Summary/Information: The UNSW School of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering has received a funding grant from ARENA to conduct a research and development project which address the performance and cost limitations of current PERC technology by transformation into PERL technology for industrial environments by incorporating multiple separately proven technologies.

Project: Integrating Industrial Black Silicon
Summary/Information: UNSW Sydney has received a funding grant from ARENA to investigate and optimise the compatibility of emerging high-throughput black silicon texturing techniques with existing and next-generation solar cell production processes.

Project: Improving World-Record Commercial High-Efficiency N-Type Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The University of New South Wales (UNSW) has received a funding grant from ARENA to conduct a project for lowering the cost and improving the efficiency of solar cell technologies using n-type silicon materials.

Project: Accelerating Industrial Solar Cells
Summary/Information: Approximately 80% of the current silicon photovoltaics production capacity is dominated by low performance cell designs whose power conversion efficiency is limited to ~20%.

Project: Manufacturing of Printed Perovskite PV Modules
Summary/Information: The Printed Perovskite PV Modules (PPV) project is developing a next-generation solar technology that has demonstrated promising performance in the laboratory. This project will translate these laboratory-scale outcomes to flexible, efficient and stable large-area PPV modules. By adopting industry-relevant approaches to materials and manufacture, the project will accelerate progress of this technology towards commercialisation.
Project partners: Monash University, University of New South Wales, University of Cambridge

Project: Efficient Adamantine Thin-Film on Silicon Tandem Cells
Summary/Information: UNSW has received a funding grant from ARENA to conduct a project targeting reduced solar cell cost, achieved by improving the efficiency with which they convert sunlight into electricity.

Project: Development of Beyond 20% Efficiency Kesterite (CZTSSe) Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Kesterite solar cell group at UNSW has received a funding grant from ARENA to develop cost-effective, high-efficiency kesterite thin-film solar cells.

Project: Tandem PV Micro Concentrator
Summary/Information: One method we use to reduce the cost of the GaAs cells is to place it at the focus of a thin plastic solar concentrator that produces tenfold concentration of sunlight on the cell. This reduces the amount of GaAs that we need by ten times. The concentrator which are the cells are mounted on a standard one-axis solar tracker – the same that is used in most large PV systems these days.
Project partners: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (​NREL), Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS)

Project: Advanced Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: A collaboration between university and industry researchers will investigate alternative methods for the deposition of thin layers of polycrystalline silicon onto silicon wafers. Such thin layers can form the junctions of the solar cell and simultaneously provide excellent passivation of its surfaces and metallic contacts. The novel technologies will be demonstrated with proof-of-concept devices, and assessed for mass production of high efficiency silicon solar cells.

Project: Next Generation Industrial Bifacial Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Next Generation Industrial Bifacial Silicon Solar Cells project brings together a consortium of ANU, GCL Technology Systems (China), and Wavelabs (Germany) to represent a complete spectrum in the PV industry encompassing R&D, manufacturing and device characterisation technologies.
Project partners: GCL System Integration Technology, Wavelabs Solar Metrology Systems GmbH

Project: Development of Stable Electrodes for Perovskite Solar Cells
Summary/Information: In this Development of Stable Electrodes for Perovskite Solar Cells project, ANU will be working with Monash University to develop new approaches for perovskite electrodes. A variety of integrated electrode structures will be developed and tested for efficiency and stability, and the cost of the developed structures will be assessed. The result is expected to be perovskite solar cells with substantially improved stability that have the potential for commercialisation.

Project: Monolithic Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Cells: Towards Commercial Reality
Summary/Information: In this project, ANU will be working with Jinko Solar to develop new approaches for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. ANU has recently achieved a world record efficiency for perovskite-silicon tandems, and together with Jinko Solar they will build on this work to produce larger, more efficient and more stable solar cells that have the potential for commercialisation.

Project: Driving Increased Efficiency and Reliability in Silicon Photovoltaics
Summary/Information: The Driving Increased Efficiency and Reliability in Silicon Photovoltaics project brings together leading research teams and industry partners from around the world to tackle the most important sources of efficiency loss in silicon solar cells. We will develop powerful new methods to identify these loss mechanisms, and new approaches to reduce their impact.
Project partners: UNSW, BT Imaging, Jinko Solar, Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems, National Renewable Energy Laboratory, Sinton Instruments, Norwegian Crystals, Topsil Global Wafers, MiaSole Hi-Tech Corp, Tesla

Project: Increasing Visibility of Distribution Networks
Summary/Information: The Increasing Visibility of Distribution Networks project developed a system that provides distribution network service providers (DNSP) with increased visibility of their medium voltage networks. The outcomes of this project are continuing to support DNSPs to take a less conservative approach in assessing and approving new customer solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to be connected to their networks.
Project partners: Queensland University of Technology, Australian Power Institute, Energy Networks Australia, Tasnetworks, United Energy, Energex Part of the Energy Queensland Group, Aurecon, Redback Technologies, Springfield City Group

Project: Monash University Polymer PV Study
Summary/Information: This project combines the expertise of researchers at Monash, Flinders, and Macquarie Universities to advance the development of all-polymer solar cells by targeting the key issues of scalability and stability.

Project: Pooled Energy Demonstration Project
Summary/Information: The Pooled Energy Demonstration Project provides retail electricity and swimming pool automation to pool owners as part of an on-going service. The energy consumption of the pools is managed from a central Network Operating Centre in such a way as to help off-load and stabilise the Grid. It is an enabling technology for intermittent renewable energy sources such as wind and sun.
Lead organisation: Pooled Energy Pty Ltd., a 100% subsidiary of Pooled Energy

Project: Powershop Australia Demand Response Program
Summary/Information: Powershop Australia’s Curb Your Power program is one of 10 pilot projects awarded funding under the demand response initiative. The Curb Your Power program will run for three years and aims to deliver a total of 5 MW of emergency reserve through behavioural change and a smartphone monitoring app.

Project: Zen Ecosystems Demand Response
Summary/Information: The Zen Ecosystems Demand Response project will see Zen Ecosystems deploy its “smart” connected thermostats across Victoria and South Australia, to aggregate and control heating and cooling within commercial and residential buildings. The project will aim to deliver 5 MW of demand response reserve from 1 December 2017, increasing to 15 MW of demand response reserve in year 3.

Project: Flow Power Energy Under Control Demand Response
Summary/Information: The Flow Power Energy Under Control Demand Response project partners with commercial and industrial businesses across New South Wales to provide strategic reserves and grid stability under the Demand Response (DR) initiative. Flow Power’s “Energy Under Control” project aims to provide an escalating reserve of 5 MW in year 1, 15 MW in year two and 20 MW in year three.
Lead organisation: Progressive Green Pty Ltd Trading As Flow Power

Project: United Energy Distribution Demand Response
Summary/Information: United Energy uses voltage control devices installed at 47 zone substations across its distribution network to deliver demand response (DR) as a participant of the Demand Response initiative. The United Energy Distribution Demand Response project delivered over 150 MW of DR reserve during the three-year trial.

Project: Enel X Demand Response Project
Summary/Information: Enel X (formerly EnerNOC), a global leader in demand response, is one of the eight companies contracted under the Demand Response initiative to trial how it can play a role in stabilising the grid in extreme peaks. Enel X is contracted to deliver 20 MW in New South Wales and 30 MW in Victoria in each of the three years of the trial.

Project: AGL Demand Response
Summary/Information: The AGL Demand Response project is one of 10 pilot projects awarded funding under ARENA and AEMO’s flagship $35.7 million Demand Response Initiative, along with support from the NSW Government.

Project: EnergyAustralia Demand Response Program
Summary/Information: The EnergyAustralia Demand Response Program (DR) program is one of 10 flagship projects supported by the joint ARENA and AEMO $35.7 million DR Initiative, along with support from the NSW Government.
Location: New South Wales, South Australia, Victoria

Project: Intercast and Forge Demand Response
Summary/Information: The Intercast and Forge Demand Response project is Australia’s largest iron casting foundry located in South Australia. IThe company has installed sophisticated energy systems that allows it to provide dispatchable demand response by powering down furnaces during peak events. The project involves the deployment of 10 MW of demand response reserve to be available for each of the three years of the trial.

Project: Perovskite Solar Cell Technology
Summary/Information: The Perovskite Solar Cell Technology project will further the prototype development phase of Greatcell Solar’s perovskite (PV) solar cell technology, following its previous ARENA feasibility study completed in 2016. This Project aims to determine that PV solar cell technology can be fabricated at industrially relevant device sizes, moving the technology along the innovation chain.

Project: HIVVE Sustainable Modular Classrooms
Summary/Information: The HIVVE Sustainable Modular Classrooms project aims to actively manage energy demands and control indoor environment quality. The 12-month trial will involve the construction and installation of a single HIVVE classroom including a monitoring and evaluation period.

Project: Roadmap for CST Power Generation in Australia
Summary/Information: A study of solar thermal technologies to develop a roadmap for Concentrated Solar Thermal power generation in Australia.

Project: Kidston Stage Two Hydro-Solar Project Activities
Summary/Information: The Kidston Stage Two Hydro-Solar Project activities project involves completing the activities required to achieve Financial Close for the Kidston Stage Two Hydro-Solar Project, which will comprise up to 270MW of solar PV and 250MW of pumped hydro. It will build on the existing 50MW solar farm already in operation.

Project: Battery of the Nation - Future State NEM Analysis Stage 1
Summary/Information: The Battery of the Nation initiative is investigating and developing a pathway of future development opportunities for Tasmania to make a greater contribution to the National Energy Market (NEM).

Project: Horizon Power Business Model Pilot Phase 1
Summary/Information: Horizon Power is conducting a pilot project to test the commercial viability of delivering decentralised, high penetration renewable energy to entire towns across regional Australia, and prove that distributed energy resources (DER) can increase renewable energy penetration on existing microgrids.

Project: Biocatalyst Optimisation & Deployment
Summary/Information: The small Australian biotechnology company Microbiogen is aiming to breed a strain of yeast that will produce a more efficient and economical form of bio-fuel from non-food sources and aim to transform the global ethanol industry.

Project: Snowy 2.0 Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Snowy 2.0 feasibility study confirms that the Snowy 2.0 pumped hydro expansion project is both technically and financially feasible.

Project: Kennedy Energy Park
Summary/Information: The Kennedy Energy Park is a hybrid renewable energy facility situated in Hughenden in North Queensland developed in a partnership between Windlab and Eurus. This project will consist of 15MW solar photovoltaic (PV), 43.2MW wind and a 2MW/4MWh lithium ion battery storage facility.

Project: Renewable Energy and Load Management Phase 1
Summary/Information: This project is about the integration and optimisation of renewable energy, onsite thermal and battery storage, energy efficiency and demand control technologies and software to create load flexibility, increasing the value and capacity to install renewable energy both on-site and across the electricity network.
Location: Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Victoria

Project: Medium-Scale Solar on Industrial Rooftops
Summary/Information: The Medium-Scale Solar on Industrial Rooftops project will complete a bankable feasibility study for the installation of approximately 11.6MW of solar on 12 industrial roof-tops in the Brisbane suburb of Eagle Farm.

Project: Battery of the Nation ' A Concept Study of Tasmanian Pumped Hydro Options
Summary/Information: The Battery of the Nation initiative is investigating and developing a pathway of future development opportunities for Tasmania to make a greater contribution to the National Energy Market.

Project: Moisture Content of Woody Biomass
Summary/Information: The cost of bioenergy production, regardless of the conversion technology and energy type produced, are highly dependent on the cost and quality of the biomass feedstock.

Project: Energy Storage for Commercial Renewable Integration (ESCRI) Phase 2
Summary/Information: The ESCRI battery is a 30 MW / 8 MWh large-scale grid-connected battery at the Dalrymple substation, Yorke Peninsula, South Australia.
Project partners: AGL (as Greentricity Pty Limited), Advisian Pty Ltd

Project: NOJA Power Intelligent Switchgear
Summary/Information: This NOJA Power Intelligent Switchgear project aims to reduce the complexity and cost of connecting renewables to the grid, and increase the hosting capacity of distribution networks by developing, demonstrating and industrialising an economical intelligent switchgear.
Project partners: AEMO, AusNet Services, Energy Queensland, Deakin University, University of Queensland

Project: Peak Demand Reduction Using Solar and Storage
Summary/Information: The Peak Demand Reduction using Solar and Storage project has successfully demonstrated a reduction in peak demand as an alternative solution for deferring network augmentation.

Project: ECLIPS Container Roll Out Solar System (CROSS)
Summary/Information: The ECLIPS Container Roll Out Solar System (CROSS) project includes the detailed design, manufacture and testing of the Container Roll Out Solar System. CROSS is a factory assembled relocatable PV solar ground array. The CROSS development includes 20ft and 40ft configurations (CROSS20 and CROSS40).

Project: Battery of the Nation
Summary/Information: The Battery of the Nation initiative is investigating and developing a pathway of future development opportunities for Tasmania to make a greater contribution to the National Energy Market (NEM). With the support of ARENA funding, Hydro Tasmania have conducted two pre-feasibility studies on the Tarraleah and Gordon hydro-electric power schemes exploring how each may be redeveloped for the future NEM.

Project: Hornsdale Wind Farm Stage 2 FCAS Trial
Summary/Information: The Hornsdale Wind Farm Stage 2 FCAS Trial project aimed to determine and demonstrate the extent of capability for wind farms of similar design and functionality to the Hornsdale Wind Farm Stage 2 (HWF2), and operating in similar conditions, to provide Frequency Controlled Ancillary Services (FCAS) to the National Electricity Market (NEM).

Project: Connecting the Power and Gas Grids
Summary/Information: The Connecting the Power and Gas Grids project aimed to design and build an electrolyser pilot plant and test it in partnership with Australian Gas Networks (AGN) as a demonstration of ‘power to gas’ injection of hydrogen into the natural gas grid.

Project: Tidal Energy in Australia
Summary/Information: The Tidal Energy in Australia project will map the country’s tidal energy resource in unprecedented detail and assess its economic feasibility and ability to contribute to Australia’s energy needs. It will aid the emerging tidal energy industry to develop commercial-scale tidal energy projects.

Project: RayGen Resources PV Ultra Commercialisation Project
Summary/Information: The RayGen PV Ultra Commercialisation Project will see RayGen Resources Pty Ltd scale up the development and deployment activities of its proprietary ‘PV Ultra’ concentrating photovoltaic technology.
Project partners: Victorian Government Department of Environment, Land, Water and Planning

Project: Comparison of Dispatchable Renewable Electricity Options
Summary/Information: ARENA commissioned a study of options for dispatchable renewable electricity generation that can support a secure, reliable and affordable electricity system with a higher share of renewable energy. The outputs are a report and a spreadsheet-based cost model.
Location: Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria, Western Australia

Project: Goulburn Bioenergy Project
Summary/Information: The Goulburn Bioenergy project is led by ReNu Energy responsible for a Bioenergy Project at the Southern Meats Facility in Goulburn NSW.

Project: Darling Downs Solar Project
Summary/Information: The Darling Downs Solar Project involves the development of a 110 MW fixed-tilt solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: EnergyAustralia South Australian (PHES) Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The EnergyAustralia South Australian (PHES) Feasibility Study project aims to determine the technical and economic feasibility of a seawater Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (PHES) plant, located south-west of Port Augusta, in South Australia.
Project partners: Arup Pty Ltd, Melbourne Energy Institute (MEI)

Project: Australian Energy Storage Council Research and Report
Summary/Information: A study of storage technologies to provide an analysis of current and future market for battery storage in Australia for use by regulators, policy makers, utilities, researchers and the energy storage industry more generally.

Project: Collinsville Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Collinsville Solar Farm Project will develop a 42.5MW (AC) solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: White Rock Solar Farm, co-located with White Rock Wind Farm
Summary/Information: The White Rock Solar project will develop a 20MW solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: SunSHIFT Pre-Commercial Deployment
Summary/Information: The project involves the fabrication of a 1 MW redeployable solar system (‘SunSHIFT’) that will be designed, constructed, ground-transported, and assembled at the South32 Cannington mine site in central Queensland.

Project: Mt Piper Power Station Energy Recovery Feasibility
Summary/Information: The Mt Piper Power Station Energy Recovery Feasibility has been completed by EnergyAustralia and the Re.Group, which assesses the viability of augmenting the 1400-megawatt (MW) Mt Piper power station near Lithgow in New South Wales with lower emissions generation.

Project: Feasibility Study for Integrated Community Waste to Energy
Summary/Information: The Feasibility Study for Integrated Community Waste to Energy project is led by the Mount Alexander Sustainability Group (MASG) to build a community waste to energy facility in Castlemaine, Victoria that would turn locally sourced organic waste into renewable energy.

Project: Whitsunday Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Whitsunday Solar Farm Project will develop a 57.5MW (AC) solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: AGL Virtual Trial of Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
Summary/Information: The AGL Virtual Trial of Peer-to-Peer (AGL VPP) Energy Trading trial sought to identify and value P2P energy trades, determine the applicability of distributed ledger technology (DLT), and analyse the results.

Project: Decentralised Energy Exchange (deX)
Summary/Information: Decentralised Energy Exchange (deX) is a prototype online marketplace that will provide a way for households and businesses with rooftop solar and battery storage systems to be paid for allowing electricity network businesses to access their rooftop solar and stored electricity to strengthen the grid.
Project partners: United Energy Distribution Pty Limited, The Australian National University, Mojo Power, ACT Environment and Planning Directorate, DELWP (Victoria), ActewAGL Distribution

Project: AGL Virtual Power Plant
Summary/Information: The AGL Virtual Power Plant is a world-leading prototype of a virtual power plants (VPP) created by installing and connecting a large number of solar battery storage systems across 1000 residential and business premises in Adelaide, South Australia, to be managed by a cloud-based control system.

Project: Adapting Renewable Energy Concepts to Irrigated Sugarcane Production
Summary/Information: The Bundaberg Regional Irrigators Group have received funding from ARENA to conduct a three year field trial to demonstrate the economic benefits of using renewable energy (specifically solar) to power irrigated sugarcane production.

Project: Parkes Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Parkes Solar Farm Project will develop a 55MW (AC) solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: Oakey Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Oakey Solar Farm project will develop a 25MW solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: Longreach Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Longreach Solar Farm is a 15MW solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: Solar Analytics: Monitoring for Better Energy Outcomes
Summary/Information: The project aims to accelerate deployment of an Australian-developed technology designed to monitor the performance of residential solar PV systems and provide low cost analytics and fault diagnostics.

Project: Manildra Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Manildra Solar Farm Project will develop a 46.7MW (AC) solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: Dubbo Solar Hub
Summary/Information: The Dubbo Solar Hub project will develop a 25MW solar photovoltaic (PV) farm. The solar farm comprises of two solar farms, Dubbo South Kenwick Solar Farm (15 MW AC) and Narromine Solar Farm (10 MW AC).
