Location: Narromine, New South Wales, South Keswick

Project: Griffith Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Griffith Solar Farm project will develop a 30MW solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: Emu Downs Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Emu Downs Solar Farm project is a 20 MW single-axis tracking solar photovoltaic (PV) farm co-located on the site of the existing 80MW Emu Downs Wind Farm.

Project: Kidston Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Kidston Solar Farm Project will develop a 50MW (AC) solar photovoltaic (PV) farm.

Project: Kidston Solar Project (Phase 1)
Summary/Information: Australia’s shift to renewable energy is picking up pace thanks to projects such as Genex Power’s 50 megawatt Kidston Solar Project (Phase One), a ground-breaking renewable energy project located in north Queensland that is creating a path to the 24/7 supply of renewable energy.
Project partners: UGL, SOLAR 120, SOCIETE GENERALE, Ergon Energy Corporation, AECOM

Project: Project Fulfil
Summary/Information: Project Fulfil will focus on delivering an affordable and reliable battery monitoring and management system for operating lead-acid batteries in partial state of charge (PSoC) applications, as well as developing interfaces and tools to enable use of the system with existing inverters, and predictive analytics to improve network integration.
Lead organisation: Smart Storage Pty Ltd (trading as Ecoult)

Project: Monash University and ClimateWorks Low Carbon Study
Summary/Information: Communicating pathways to deep decarbonisation through electric vehicles and renewable energy technologies.

Project: Tidal Turbine Reef Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Tidal Turbine Reef Feasibility Study aims to test the viability of a novel ‘Tidal Turbine Reef’ (TTR) generator from technical, environmental, social and financial standpoints, to determine whether it can achieve an economically viable Levelised Cost of Electricity (LCOE).
Project partners: Tenax, SCHOTTEL HYDRO GmbH, Ecofin Solutions, Curtin University, Civmec

Project: Narara Ecovillage Smart Grid
Summary/Information: The Narara Ecovillage Smart Grid project aims to balance the energy generation, consumption and storage in a new development, initially of 50 houses.
Project partners: NEV Power, Carbon Neutral Delivery Partners

Project: Unitywater Sewage Waste to Energy Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: The Unitywater Sewage Waste to Energy Feasibility Study project will assess the commercial viability of converting Unitywater’s Kawana sewage treatment facility on the Sunshine Coast to generate biogas and electricity from a variety of waste sources.

Project: Networks Renewed
Summary/Information: The Networks Renewed project investigated pathways to increase the amount of renewable energy in Australia by paving the way for small-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery storage installations to improve the quality and reliability of electricity in Australia’s distribution networks.
Project partners: Reposit Power, Essential Energy, AusNet Services, Australian PV Institute, United Energy

Project: UNSW Addressing Barriers to Efficient Renewable Integration
Summary/Information: The UNSW Addressing Barriers to Efficient Renewable Integration project is identifying and addressing the roadblocks to having high degrees of renewable energy deployment related to system integration.

Project: Garden Island Microgrid Project
Summary/Information: The Garden Island Microgrid Project plans to be the world’s first wave energy integrated microgrid and will produce both power and desalinated water.

Project: Solar Field Chilling and Heating Opportunities in a Hospital Environment
Summary/Information: The primary objective of the project is to facilitate a case study, prepared by CSIRO, on the integration of solar thermal technology at the hospital.

Project: Atlas of Pumped Hydro Energy Storage
Summary/Information: The Atlas of Pumped Hydro Energy Storage project will assess the potential for Short Term Off-River pumped hydro Energy Storage (STORES) to provide cost-effective storage on a large scale in Australia, supporting higher levels of renewable energy in the National Electricity Market and South West Interconnected System.
Project partners: ElectraNet, CWP Renewables, AvensolSolar, Australian PV Institute

Project: Lakeland Solar and Storage Project
Summary/Information: The Lakeland Solar and Storage Project project involves the construction of a large-scale solar plant with battery storage in the Lakeland region of North Queensland. The integration of big solar and battery storage has the potential to revolutionise power supply for fringe-of-grid locations.
Lead organisation: Lakeland Solar & Storage Pty Limited, a subsidiary of Conergy

Project: Promoting Use of Solar Cooling and Heating in Australia (PUSCH)
Summary/Information: This project is about capacity building and knowledge sharing, to support the Australian building industry to adopt solar cooling and heating technologies through training, Australian case studies and various knowledge dissemination activities. This project delivered an industry roadmap to overcome barriers and assist with market transformation.
Project partners: Australian Institute of Refrigeration, Air conditioning and Heating

Project: Utilising Biogas in Sugarcane Transport and Milling
Summary/Information: Australia’s sugar industry is worth more than $2 billion per year and is the third largest exporter of raw sugar globally. While the industry produces considerable renewable energy (electricity and steam) from bagasse, this Utilising Biogas in Sugarcane Transport and Milling project will explore opportunities exist to utilise sugarcane trash, or field residues remaining after harvesting. This is currently considered to be an uneconomic way of generating energy.
Project partners: Utilitas Pty Ltd, Sunshine Sugar, Griffith University

Project: Expansion of the Environmental Upgrade Agreement Market
Summary/Information: This project enabled the expansion of the commercial rooftop solar market across Victoria by increasing the number of local governments offering innovative finance for such projects where loan repayments are made via Council rates.

Project: Pilot Landfill Solar Project
Summary/Information: The Pilot Landfill Solar Project is a pilot scale photovoltaic (PV) installation to determine the feasibility of installing solar PV at a landfill site.

Project: Integrating Concentrating Solar Thermal Energy
Summary/Information: The Integrating Concentrating Solar Thermal Energy project will evaluate the potential for energy produced from concentrating solar thermal (CST) technologies to be integrated into the Bayer alumina refining process. It will develop the technologies and process knowledge to enable the progressive integration of low temperature CST, solar reforming of natural gas, and high temperature CST into the existing Bayer process.
Project partners: UNSW Australia, San Diego State University, IT Power Australia Pty Ltd, Hatch Associates Pty Ltd, ETH Zurich, CSIRO, Alcoa of Australia Limited

Project: Real-Time Operational PV Simulations
Summary/Information: The Real-Time Operational PV Simulations project provided low voltage network operators (DNSPs) with high resolution solar energy forecasting data mapped to their electricity networks.
Project partners: Soly, Solar Hub, SMA, Si Clean Energy, Regional Power Corporation, Power and Water Corporation, Essential Energy, Ergon Energy Corporation, Electricity Networks Corporation

Project: Consumer Energy Systems Providing Cost-Effective Grid Support
Summary/Information: The CONSORT Bruny Island Battery Trial successfully developed and demonstrated an innovative automated control platform that enables consumers with battery systems to provide support to a constrained electricity network. It continues to do so in a way that is of maximum benefit to both the consumer and the network.
Project partners: TasNetworks, Reposit Power, University of Sydney, University of Tasmania​

Project: Robotic Vision System for Automatic Inspection & Evaluation of Solar Plants
Summary/Information: The Robotic vision system project will develop a cost-effective robotic inspection system for automated monitoring of concentrating solar power and solar photovoltaic power plants using cameras mounted on ground and aerial drones.
Project partners: White Knight Unmanned Arial Systems PTY LTD, Vast Solar Pty Ltd, NICTA, FRV Services Australia Pty Ltd

Project: Increasing the Uptake of Solar PV in Strata Residential Developments
Summary/Information: The Increasing the Uptake of Solar PV in Strata Residential Developments project will develop governance models to allow shared solar photovoltaics (PV), battery and monitoring systems to be used in medium density apartments. The governance models will be tested at 50 units of the White Gum Valley development in Perth.
Project partners: LandCorp, Electricity Networks Corporation, CRC for Low Carbon Living, City of Fremantle, Balance Utility Solutions

Project: Smart Sodium Storage System
Summary/Information: The Smart Sodium Storage System project will develop and integrate a new type of sodium-ion battery in a low-cost, modular and expandable energy storage system to be demonstrated at the Illawarra Flame House and Sydney Water’s Bondi Sewage Pumping Station.
Project partners: Sydney Water, Nano-Nouvelle, McNair, Liao Ning Hong Cheng Electric Power Co, Hebei ANZ New Energy Technology Company

Project: Maximising Solar PV with Phase Change Thermal Energy Storage
Summary/Information: The Maximising Solar PV with Phase Change Thermal Energy Storage project developed a low cost, phase change material (PCM) for the industrial and commercial refrigeration market, and also to optimise the control and operation of PCM thermal storage systems integrated with solar photovoltaics (PV).
Project partners: University of Lleida, The Solar Project, Glaciem

Project: Wave Energy Cost Reduction
Summary/Information: The Wave Energy Cost Reduction project will involve investigating the optimal number, size, arrangement and location of wave energy device arrays to minimise the cost of installation and infrastructure while maximising power output.

Project: TransGrid New England Renewable Hub (REHub) Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: A feasibility study on the establishment of a connection hub for potential renewable energy operators in the New England region in northern New South Wales to connect to the grid.

Project: Northern Oil Advanced Biofuels Laboratory
Summary/Information: The Northern Oil Advanced Biofuels Laboratory project involves the development and construction of Australia’s first biocrude and biofuel laboratory at the site of the Northern Oil Advanced Biofuels Pilot Plant in Yarwun, central Queensland.
Lead organisation: Southern Oil Refining Pty Ltd (Southern Oil Refining or SOR)

Project: Kidston Pumped Storage Project
Summary/Information: The Kidston Pumped Storage Project is a feasibility study into the construction of a pumped storage hydroelectric power plant at the disused Kidston Gold Mine in North Queensland.

Project: Australian Biomass for Bioenergy Assessment 2015-2021
Summary/Information: The Australian Biomass for Bioenergy Assessment Project recognises that previous biomass resource mapping has either been undertaken at a regionally specific scale or is incomplete. The lack of reliable information on biomass feedstocks is a significant roadblock to the development of bioenergy projects across Australia.
Lead organisation: Rural Industries Research and Development Corporation
Project partners: University of the Sunshine Coast, Sustainability Victoria, Renewables SA, Queensland University of Technology, Department of State Growth, Department of Science, Information Technology and Innovation, Department of Primary Industries, Department of Agriculture and Food (WA)

Project: Normanton Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Normanton Solar Farm project will involve the construction of the 5MW DC Normanton Solar Farm in North-West Queensland.
Project partners: SMEC, Normanton Solar Farm, CEFC, Canadian Solar (Australia) Pty Limited

Project: Specifying Guidelines for Assessing Next Generation Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project will establish guidelines for measuring the performance of emerging photovoltaic (PV) technologies such as perovskite solar cells. The guidelines will help to ensure Australian research laboratories have access to a best practice methodology that is reliable, transferable and accurately reflects the true performance of the devices in the outdoor environment.

Project: Energy Cost Study for Bombora Wave Energy Converter
Summary/Information: The Bombora ‘Cost of Energy Study’ (Study) detailed the ‘cost of electricity’ for energy produced by a 60MW mWave™ wave farm, and confirmed the potential commercial viability of the mWave wave energy converter technology as a source of renewable energy.

Project: Pentland Bioenergy Project
Summary/Information: The Pentland Bioenergy Project will determine the technical and commercial viability of Australia’s largest integrated biofuel facility, proposed for construction at Pentland, near Charters Towers in North Queensland.
Project partners: De Smet Engineers & Contractors SA, Beta-Renewables

Project: Geothermal Structural Permeability Map
Summary/Information: The Geothermal Structural Permeability Map project delivered a national database and map of natural fractures and subsurface permeability in critical Australian basins to better exploit geothermal resources across Australia.
Lead organisation: University of Adelaide (South Australian Centre for Geothermal Energy Research)

Project: Moreland Micro-Grid Investigation
Summary/Information: The Moreland Micro-Grid Investigation project will examine the logistical, regulatory and financial challenges facing the adoption of micro-grids in existing suburbs.

Project: Commercialisation Roadmap for Perovskite Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is designed to deliver a ‘commercialisation roadmap’ that supports Dyesol’s ambition to move to scalable manufacturing of efficient and reliable perovskite solar cell technology.

Project: Establishing the Basis for Industrial Development
Summary/Information: The project reported that perovskite solar cells (PSC) were both efficient and stable, confirming the potential viability and cost-competitiveness of PSC technology for commercial-scale manufacture.

Project: Higher Renewable Penetration in New Land & Housing Developments
Summary/Information: This project aims to explore the commercial viability and impact of renewable energy for large new housing developments with off-grid microgrids.

Project: Central Receiver CPV Pilot Project Stage 3
Summary/Information: This project will develop designs to commercialise the world’s only ‘power tower’ system that uses solar photovoltaic (PV) receivers to generate renewable energy from concentrated sunlight.

Project: Trialling a New Residential Solar PV and Battery Model
Summary/Information: The Trialling a New Residential Solar PV and Battery Model project involves Queensland energy provider Ergon Retail undertaking a pilot demonstration to test a commercial and operational model for providing grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery storage systems to residential customers.
Lead organisation: Ergon Energy Queensland Pty Ltd (Ergon Retail)

Project: Karratha Airport Solar Plant
Summary/Information: The Karratha Airport Solar Plant project involves the design, construction, commissioning and operation of a 1 MW solar photovoltaic (PV) facility with cloud predictive technology (CPT) at Western Australia’s second-largest airport Karratha Airport. The City of Karratha, which owns Karratha Airport, will enter into a 21 year power purchase agreement (PPA) with the solar plant.

Project: Toolkit for Community Renewable Energy Funding and Financing
Summary/Information: Frontier Impact Group will develop a financial toolkit for funding and financing community energy projects. A central repository will house simplified information on obtaining finance throughout each phase of the development process including concept, pre-feasibility, feasibility and financial close.
Project partners: Trading as Community Power Agency, Embark Australia

Project: Investigating Local Network Charges and Local Electricity Trading
Summary/Information: Network businesses do not currently offer a tariff to reflect partial use of the network and retailers do not currently offer a standard netting off service, called local electricity trading (previously known as virtual net metering), for multiple sites.
Lead organisation: Institute for Sustainable Futures, University of Technology, Sydney

Project: Energy Storage Test Facility and Knowledge Bank
Summary/Information: University of Adelaide will build a mobile energy storage test facility and establish an online database for Australian energy storage expertise.
Project partners: Zen Energy Systems, South Australian Govt DMITRE, Solar Storage, SA Power Networks, Power and Drive Solutions, Energy Networks Association

Project: Rottnest Island Water and Renewable Energy Nexus (WREN) Project
Summary/Information: The Rottnest Island Water and Renewable Energy Nexus (WREN) project offers an inspiring example of how innovative deployment of hybrid renewables can increase the power supply security and sustainability of an off-grid island and drive water desalination.

Project: Testing the Performance of Lithium Ion Batteries
Summary/Information: The Testing the Performance of Lithium Ion Batteries project analyses the performance of twenty-six leading batteries, comparing major lithium-ion battery brands to existing and advanced lead-acid battery technologies, as well as a zinc-bromide flow battery and a sodium-nickel chloride battery.

Project: Clean Energy Australia Annual Renewable Energy Industry Analysis
Summary/Information: This project will provide funding support for the Clean Energy Council to produce the Clean Energy Australia Report 2014.

Project: Yulara Solar Project
Summary/Information: The Yulara Solar Project, commissioned in March 2016, integrates 1.8 MW of solar photovoltaics (PV) into the existing power system at the Yulara Resort near the iconic Uluru in the Northern Territory.

Project: Predicting Cloud Movements to Maximise Solar PV Use
Summary/Information: The Predicting Cloud Movements to Maximise Solar PV Use project involves the development and demonstration of a sophisticated cloud tracking solution. Fulcrum3D’s ‘CloudCAM’ technology is expected to perform better than existing optical sky cameras in identifying cloud height and separating out layered clouds.

Project: Flinders Island Hybrid Energy Hub
Summary/Information: The project aims to use a combination of solar, wind, diesel, storage and enabling technologies to displace more than 60% of Flinders Island’s diesel generated energy. Hydro Tasmania will develop a modular hybrid energy solution with the potential to further drive down costs and move a step closer to delivering a commercially competitive product.

Project: Solar and Storage Trial at Alkimos Beach Residential Development
Summary/Information: The Solar and Storage Trial at Alkimos Beach Residential Development project involves developing, deploying and testing the commercial feasibility of a new energy retail model. It will combine community scale battery storage, high penetration rooftop solar PV and energy management within a new residential development at Alkimos Beach, Western Australia.
Project partners: Lendlease Communities (Alkimos) Pty Ltd , Synergy, Development WA

Project: Energy Storage for Commercial Renewable Integration
Summary/Information: The Energy Storage for Commercial Renewable Integration (ESCRI) project examined the role of medium to large scale (5-30MW) energy storage in the integration of renewable energy into the South Australian electricity system.

Project: Australian Renewable Energy Mapping Infrastructure Project
Summary/Information: The Australian Renewable Energy Mapping Infrastructure Project (AREMI) is being developed to share mapping data and information with the renewable energy industry. The mapping platform is being developed by CSIRO’s Data61, Australia’s Centre of Excellence in Information and Communication Technology Research and Development.

Project: Renewable Energy Excellence Industry Cluster
Summary/Information: The Renewable Energy Excellence Industry Cluster is being led by Regional Development Australia ACT (RDA ACT) to establish a Regional Renewable Energy Industry Cluster in the south east NSW-ACT region as part of the South East Region of Renewable Energy Excellence (SERREE) initiative.
Project partners: Zhenfa Australia Pty Ltd, Windlab Systems Pty Ltd, Vestas, Union Fenosa Wind Australia, Senvion, Regional Development Australia Southern Inland, NSW Government OEH, NSW Department of Trade and Investment, Infigen

Project: Ocean Wave-Power Machines
Summary/Information: Swinburne University of Technology has developed modelling on the performance of wave energy farms. The research identified the impact of Wave Energy Converters on each other in an array, and the impact of current flows in these arrays.
Lead organisation: Swinburne University of Technology, Centre for Ocean Engineering, Science and Technology

Project: High Efficiency Solar Thermal Power Using Allam Cycle
Summary/Information: The High Efficiency Solar Thermal Power Using Allam Cycle project builds on CSIRO’s existing solar work in high temperature and high pressure power cycles, including supercritical CO2. It involves partnering with industry and research organisations to develop the components, materials and processes necessary to progress this technology to a commercial-scale system.
Project partners: Toshiba International, National Renewable Energy Labs, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Abengoa Solar Power Australia, 8 Rivers

Project: Improving Solar Cell Performance Testing
Summary/Information: The Improving Solar Cell Performance Testing project investigated factors that can deteriorate solar cell performance, using an innovative measurement system in combination with advanced simulation tools.
Project partners: The Australian National University, Sinton Instruments, BT Imaging

Project: Creating a Better Solar Cell
Summary/Information: Perovskite cells have only emerged as a viable photovoltaic material over the past two years. The Creating a Better Solar Cell project was the first time a tandem, stacked approach has been attempted with silicon cells on this scale.
Project partners: Trina Solar Ltd, The Australian National University, Suntech R&D Australia Pty Ltd, Monash University, Arizona State University

Project: Towards Ultimate Performance Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Ultimate Performance Silicon Solar Cells project recognises that new solar cell structures and production processes have the potential to further reduce the cost and increase the performance of commercial photovoltaic (PV) solar cells.
Project partners: Yingli Green Energy Holding Co. Ltd, Trina Solar Ltd, Tempress Systems, Suntech R&D Australia Pty Ltd, Sunrise Global Solar Energy, Sharesun Co. Ltd, SCHMID Group | Gebr. SCHMID GmbH, Roth & Rau AG, Hyundai Heavy industries Co Ltd

Project: DeGrussa Solar Project
Summary/Information: The project consists of a 10.6 MW (AC) solar PV power plant with storage at the DeGrussa Copper Mine.
Project partners: Sandfire Resources NL, juwi Renewable Energy, Juwi AG

Project: Barcaldine Remote Community Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Barcaldine Remote Community Solar Farm (BRCSF) will be located in central Queensland within a fringe-of-grid area of super-premium solar irradiation. The project site is approximately 90 hectares and located near the Barcaldine Gas Power Plant.

Project: Mapping Network Opportunities for Renewable Energy
Summary/Information: The Mapping Network Opportunities for Renewable Energy project will create online maps of electricity network constraints to help better inform network investments and increase the use of renewable energy.
Project partners: NSW Trade and Investment, Ergon Energy Corporation, ElectraNet, Clean Energy Council Ltd.

Project: Novel Concepts for Low Cost Small Heliostats in Remote Installations
Summary/Information: The Novel Concepts for Low Cost Small Heliostats in Remote Installations project developed a heliostat optimised for deployment in regional and remote areas of Australia. A heliostat is a device used for harnessing the sun’s energy that includes a mirror which moves with the sun to continuously reflect light toward a fixed target.
Project partners: Rioglass Solar International, Diver Consolidated Industries

Project: Virtual Power Station 2
Summary/Information: The Virtual Power Station 2 project builds on CSIRO’s existing research, creating the next version of a virtual power station (VPS2) that can undertake pilot-scale testing of load, generation and energy storage coordination.
Project partners: University of Newcastle, Tritium Pty Ltd, SMA, Selectronic Australia Pty Ltd, Lend Lease Communities (Australia) Ltd., Latronic Sunpower Ltd., Ergon Energy Corporation

Project: Future Proofing in Australia's Electricity Distribution Industry
Summary/Information: The Future Proofing in Australia’s Electricity Distribution Industry project aims to enhance the flexibility and resilience of Australia’s electricity distribution system. The Clean Energy Council will conduct extensive consultations with industry, government, regulators and consumers, and commission technical, economic and regulatory analysis

Project: Lord Howe Island Hybrid Renewable Energy System
Summary/Information: The Lord Howe Island Hybrid Renewable Project will add more than 1.2 MW of renewable energy generating capacity and over 3.2 MWh of battery storage to the current diesel power generation system operating on Lord Howe Island, NSW.
Location: Lord Howe Island, New South Wales

Project: Doomadgee Solar Project
Summary/Information: This project aims to demonstrate the technical viability and system reliability of a hybrid electricity system involving a large amount of solar photovoltaic (PV) energy with diesel generation. The project will integrate 1.26 MW of solar PV generation into the existing diesel power station that powers the Doomadgee community in remote Queensland.

Project: NT Solar Energy Transformation Program
Summary/Information: The NT Solar Energy Transformation Program (SETuP) has transformed the delivery of electricity in remote off-grid communities throughout the Northern Territory.
Lead organisation: Power and Water Corporation Indigenous Essential Services Pty Ltd

Project: Gullen Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Gullen Solar Farm project is a 10 megawatt (MW) solar farm co located with Gullen Range Wind Farm 30km north west of Goulburn in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales.

Project: Asia-Pacific Solar Research Conference 2014
Summary/Information: The 2014 Asia-Pacific Solar Research Conference was held on the 8 – 10 Dec 2014 at the Colombo Theatres, University of New South Wales, Sydney.

Project: Intelligent Storage for Australia's Grid
Summary/Information: The Intelligent Storage for Australia’s Grid project involves piloting GridCredits, a battery storage control module that allows consumers to monitor electricity usage and access their solar power overnight and at peak times.

Project: High-Temperature Solar Thermal Energy Storage
Summary/Information: This project aimed to develop an innovative energy storage system that uses concentrating solar thermal technology to drive a high-temperature redox (or reduction-oxidation) thermochemical cycle.
Project partners: University of Colorado Boulder, IT Power Australia Pty Ltd

Project: Improving Solar Thermal Receivers for Reduced Heat Loss
Summary/Information: This project investigated novel configurations of tube banks for central tower receivers, including bladed concepts and incorporating the use of active airflow techniques.
Project partners: The University of Adelaide, Sandia National Laboratories, CSIRO

Project: Advanced Surface and Contact Technologies Improving Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Advanced Surface and Contact Technologies Improving Solar Cells project aims to develop a suite of key cell process technologies to improve the surface of silicon solar cells.
Project partners: UNSW Australia, Trina Solar, Tempress Systems

Project: Lowering the Cost of High Efficiency Silicon Solar Panels
Summary/Information: The Lowering the Cost of High Efficiency Silicon Solar Panels project will identify and reduce the impact of defects and impurities throughout the solar panel production process. It will cover the initial growth of the silicon ingots, wafers, cells and the final panel.
Project partners: UNSW Australia, University of Warwick, SunEdison, Sinton Instruments, Institut für Solarenergieforschung Hameln/Emmerthal GmbH, Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems, BT Imaging, Apollon Solar

Project: Solar Panels for the Australian Environment
Summary/Information: The Solar Panels for the Australian Environment recognises that designing a PV module for Australian conditions is a complex and difficult engineering task, requiring modification of almost all module components.
Project partners: UNSW Australia, Tindo Solar, Sunpulse K. K., PV Lighthouse, PV LAB AUSTRALIA PTY LTD, Brisbane Materials Technology Pty Ltd

Project: Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Large-Scale Energy Storage
Summary/Information: The Lithium-Sulfur Batteries for Large-Scale Energy Storage project aimed to develop advanced lithium-sulfur batteries for renewable energy storage with high-energy density, extended service life and operational safety.
Project partners: Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute, Ergon Energy Corporation, DLG Battery

Project: Re-Deployable Hybrid Power (Sunshift)
Summary/Information: The Re-Deployable Hybrid Power (Sunshift) project involved a pilot-scale deployment of a fully re-deployable hybrid solar/diesel power plant that has the potential to change the renewable energy landscape in regional and remote Australia. Laing O’Rourke successfully operate and removed this demonstration plant in March 2015.

Project: Woody Biomass Harvester
Summary/Information: This project involves the design, construction and testing of an innovative woody biomass harvester

Project: Low Emission Biofuel Technology
Summary/Information: Researchers in Curtin University’s Fuels and Energy Technology Institute have developed a new technology that converts biomass such as mallee crops into biofuels and biochar via biomass conversion (pyrolysis) and biorefinement.
Project partners: Oil Mallee Association of Australia, Curtin University

Project: Coober Pedy Renewable Diesel Hybrid
Summary/Information: The Coober Pedy Renewable Diesel Hybrid project aimed to install 1MW solar, 4MW wind generation, a 1MW, 0.5MWh battery storage and inverter system as well as a range of additional proven technologies, integrated with Energy Developments Ltd’s (EDL) existing 3.9MW diesel power station in Coober Pedy.

Project: Australian Wave Energy Atlas
Summary/Information: This project has developed an atlas that makes it easier to assess the feasibility of wave power projects.
Project partners: Australian Maritime College - The University of Tasmania, Bureau of Meteorology, BioPower Systems, Carnegie Clean Energy, Swinburne University of Technology

Project: International Energy Agency's Bioenergy Program
Summary/Information: The International Energy Agency’s Bioenergy Program project involves Bioenergy Australia extending its participation in the International Energy Agency’s Bioenergy program. It will help shape the global research and knowledge agenda for the developing bioenergy industry.
Project partners: University of the Sunshine Coast, University of Southern Queensland, University of New England, Monash University, BioIndustry Partners Pty Ltd

Project: Carnegie CETO 6 Technology
Summary/Information: This demonstration project will design, install and operate a grid connected CETO 6 unit off the coast of Albany, Western Australia. Albany has one of the most consistent wave energy resources in the world.

Project: Pathways to Deep Decarbonisation in 2050
Summary/Information: This project explores the role of renewable energy technologies and biofuels in decarbonising the Australian economy. The project is jointly led by ClimateWorks Australia and the Australian National University and draws on the latest research and modelling by CSIRO and Centre of Policy Studies at Victoria University.
Lead organisation: ClimateWorks Australia and the Australian National University (project co-leaders)

Project: Investigating a Bioenergy Alternative for Mines
Summary/Information: ARENA provided $300,000 to lay the groundwork for a renewable biogas project in the Pilbara. The Investigating a Bioenergy Alternative for Mines project found that it is technically feasible to supply remote mine sites with electricity and/or natural gas produced from purpose grown biomass using mine dewatering using Anaerobic Digestion.

Project: Future-Proofing in the Electricity Distribution Industry
Summary/Information: A study of enabling technologies to future-proof Australia’s Electricity Distribution Industry.

Project: Weipa 6.7MW Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Weipa Solar Farm project will construct and operate a 6.7MW solar photovoltaic (PV) solar farm in two stages at Rio Tinto’s remote bauxite operation in Weipa. The system will connect to Rio Tinto’s existing mini-grid at Weipa and deliver electricity according to a long term Power Purchase Agreement (PPA).

Project: Feasibility Study for Perenjori 20MW Dispatchable Solar Tower
Summary/Information: The Perenjori 20MW Dispatchable Solar Tower project is a feasibility study into the construction of a 20 MWe solar thermal power station in Perenjori, WA. The plant would employ Abengoa’s molten salt tower technology with a thermal energy storage system and would be integrated into the north-eastern fringe of WA’s South Western Interconnected System (SWIS).

Project: Re-Deployable Hybrid Power Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: This project involves a feasibility study into a portable hybrid solar/diesel power plant. Laing O’Rourke will undertake the study, which has the potential to change the renewable energy landscape in regional and remote Australia.

Project: CSP Pilot Plant
Summary/Information: In 2012 Vast Solar commenced its 1.2 MW Performance Validation Project which was supported by funding from the then Australian Solar Institute. This involved a single module of Vast Solar’s low-cost, high-performance concentrating solar thermal (CST) power system – a solar field of 700 mirrors focused on a single tower with a thermal energy receiver.

Project: Port Augusta Solar Thermal Feasibility Study
Summary/Information: This project focused on the pre-feasibility work needed to assess the viability of a stand-alone solar thermal plant using ‘power tower’ technology that would see a field of mirrors concentrate light into a central receiver at the top of a tower. The high temperatures generated by power tower technology make it most compatible with molten-salt storage.

Project: National Community Energy Strategy
Summary/Information: The project also developed National Community Energy Strategy; the National Community Energy Strategy contains strategies that focus on addressing the challenges and opportunities unique to community-owned renewable energy projects.

Project: Australian Involvement in the IEA PV Power Systems
Summary/Information: A study of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to enhance Australian involvement in the International Energy Agency PV power systems, and solar heating and cooling implementing agreements.

Project: Self Patterning Dielectric Metal Nanostructure
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate self-patterning dielectric/metal nanostructures at the rear surface of silicon solar cells for advanced passivation and light trapping.

Project: VISY Clean Energy Project
Summary/Information: A study of bioenergy technologies to support technical innovations and approvals process for the Visy Clean Energy Project in Sydney and Tumut.

Project: Fabrication of High Performance Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to optimise the selective emitter fabrication process using laser technology.

Project: AGL Solar Project
Summary/Information: The AGL Solar Project aimed to increase knowledge in large-scale solar energy through the construction of two solar photovoltaic (PV) power stations in New South Wales. Combined, the projects generate up to 155 megawatts (MW) (AC) of electricity.
Location: Broken Hill and Nyngan, New South Wales
Project partners: NSW Office of Environment and Heritage, Australian Renewable Energy Agency

Project: Lateral Optimisation of Dye-Sensitised Thin Film Photovoltaics
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop lateral optimisation of dye-sensitised thin film photovoltaics.

Project: Reducing the Cost of Solar Power by Thin-Film Engineering Strategies
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to improve cost reduction of photovoltaic power generation, through thin-film engineering strategies applied to crystalline silicon photovoltaic devices and modules.

Project: Guiding the Rational Design of Organic Dye Sensitisers
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop an experimental and theoretical approach to the design of organic dye sensitisers for solar cell technologies.

Project: Investigation of Aluminium Alloys
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to investigate aluminium alloys as phase change materials for concentrated solar power plants running supercritical CO2 power cycles.

Project: Flexible Barrier Encapsulation for Printed Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate flexible barrier encapsulation for printed solar cells.

Project: Development of Low Bandgap Polymeric Acceptors
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop low bandgap polymeric acceptors for organic solar cells.

Project: High Efficiency N-Type Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to fabricate high efficiency n-type silicon solar cells with local laser doping by laser chemical processing.

Project: Thermal Evaporation of High Efficiency Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a process to reliably produce high efficiency copper-zinc-tin-sulphide (CZTS) solar cells.

Project: Nanosphere Lithography for Controlled Fabrication of Plasmonic Films
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop nanosphere lithography for controlled fabrication of large-area plasmonic films.

Project: Characterisation of Light Distribution within Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate light distributions within various types of solar cells.

Project: Singlet Heterofission in Organic Dimers
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate organic molecules for use in organic photovoltaic devices.

Project: Generation Investment and Policy Support Frameworks
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to provide theoretical framework and analysis tools for facilitating high solar generation penetrations in Australia’s electricity industry.

Project: Novel Solution-Processed Multilayer D-I-A Organic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a novel solution-processed multilayer donor/ionic species/acceptor organic solar cell.

Project: Integration of High Efficient Photon Up-Conversion Systems
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to integrate high efficiency photon up-conversion systems with organic solar cells for third generation PV applications.

Project: High Quality Laser Doping for Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project developed innovative characterisation (measurement) approaches that allow high quality data to be collected quickly and accurately, thereby providing a way to rapidly improve laser doping.

Project: Advanced & Industry-Ready Photo-Characterisation of Silicon Bricks
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop new photoluminescence imaging based methods for silicon bricks inspection for advanced and industry-ready manufacturing.

Project: Development of Novel Nanocluster-Based Buffer Layers
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop novel nanocluster-based buffer layers for multi-junction solar cells.

Project: Moree Solar Farm
Summary/Information: The Moree Solar Farm uses solar photovoltaic-polycrystalline modules and a single-axis horizontal tracking system which allows the modules to follow the sun to maximise power output.

Project: Transparent and Conductive Graphene/Polymer Thin Films
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to fabricate novel transparency, conductive and flexible graphene/polymer thin films, with targeted applications in organic photovoltaics.

Project: Inkjet Enabled Silicon Solar Cell Fabrication
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to refine and further develop inkjet patterning processes for silicon solar cells developed at UNSW to establish their manufacturability.

Project: Singlet Exciton Fission and Multiexciton Harvesting in Organic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to advance the efficiency of organic solar cells beyond established thermodynamic limits.

Project: Nanostructures Design for Light Trapping
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to design nanostructures with optimal light trapping in silicon wafer and chalcogenide thin-film solar cells.

Project: Photovoltaic-Powered Ultraviolet Light Emitting Diode Water
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate the feasibility and design of point of use, low energy, photovoltaic-powered ultraviolet light emitting diode for water disinfection.

Project: Impact of Spin on Fundamental Optoelectronic Processes
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate the impact of spin on fundamental optoelectronic processes in organic semiconductors.

Project: Producing Advanced Drop-In Fuels for Australia
Summary/Information: This project undertook a feasibility study into the construction and operation of a pre-commercial biofuels plant that converts inedible plant material (biomass) into a bio-crude oil with similar characteristics to traditional fossil crude.

Project: UltraBattery Distributed PV Support
Summary/Information: This project will apply CSIRO’s breakthrough UltraBattery technology to deliver superior energy storage solutions.
Lead organisation: Smart Storage Pty Ltd T/A Ecoult

Project: Copper-Zinc-Tin-Sulfide Thin-Film Solar Cell
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a prototype copper-zinc-tin-sulfide (CZTS) thin-film solar cell on stainless steel substrate for application and commercialisation.

Project: Tools for Design and Scale-up of Solar Thermochemical Reactors
Summary/Information: The Tools for Design and Scale-up of Solar Thermochemical Reactors project will produce the basic knowledge needed to design solar thermochemical reactors that can perform required energy conversions.

Project: Future Fuels Program
Advancing Marine Microalgae Biofuel to Commercialisation
Summary/Information: Australia and the broader global community are searching for viable, sustainable alternatives to fossil oil as future sources of liquid fuels, and to develop superior solutions to biofuels currently produced from food crops such as corn-based ethanol and biodiesel from palm oil.

Project: Australian Solar Energy Forecasting System - Phase 1
Summary/Information: This project delivered the Australian Solar Energy Forecasting System (ASEFS), which uses basic techniques to cover all the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) required forecasting timeframes for managing the National Electricity Market (NEM), which range from five minutes to two years.

Project: Conversion of Coal to Hybrid Solar Thermal/Gas
Summary/Information: This project assessed the viability of converting the existing 180 MW coal-fired Collinsville Power Station in Queensland to a 30 MW hybrid solar thermal/gas power station. It was ultimately determined that a project was not feasible at the current time due to excessive capital costs.
Project partners: Transfield Infrastructure Pty Ltd, University of Queensland

Project: High Efficiency Low Cost Silicon Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high efficiency, low cost silicon cells with anodically grown silicon dioxide films.

Project: Time-Resolved Microspectroscopy of Conjugated Polymer Films
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to improve organic photovoltaic technologies using cutting edge microscopic and spectroscopic techniques.

Project: Institutional Rigidity in the National Electricity Market
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to investigate the extent to which institutional arrangements in the Australian national electricity market facilitate the integration of technologies and network adaptation.

Project: Hybrid PV-T Static Micro Concentrators
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a hybrid PV-T static microconcentrator based on non-imaging optics.

Project: Integration of Renewables into Power Systems
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to investigate integration of renewables into power systems, including the energy market.

Project: Practical Realisation of a Hot Carrier Solar Cell Using Hafnium Nitride
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a hot carrier solar cell using hafnium nitride.

Project: Ultra-thin Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop ultra-thick silicon solar cells fabricated on steel substrates to deliver high conversion efficiencies.

Project: Optimising Concentrated Solar Thermal Operation
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to optimise concentrated solar thermal operation using solar energy forecasting.

Project: High Temperature Stainless Steels for Concentrated Solar Power
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to investigate and develop new high temperature alloys for concentrated solar thermal receivers for solar power towers.

Project: Novel Texture Processes for the Latest Industrial Wafer
Summary/Information: Wafer texturing is one of the first steps in creating a solar cell from a silicon wafer. The texturing roughens or etches the solar cell surface, to improve the cell’s performance by reducing light lost from reflection and trapping light in the solar cell.

Project: Ultrafast Spectroscopy for Third Generation Photovoltaics
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate ultrafast spectroscopy for third generation photovoltaics.

Project: ASTRI Australian Solar Thermal Research Institute
Summary/Information: The ASTRI Australian Solar Thermal Research Institute is a consortium of leading Australian research institutions collaborating on ‘over the horizon’ concentrating solar power (CSP) research projects.
Project partners: Australian National University, The University of Queensland, The University of Adelaide, Queensland University of Technology, University of South Australia, Flinders University

Project: Utility-Scale Solar Installations
Summary/Information: The Utility-Scale Solar Installations project involved undertaking comprehensive research to develop an understanding of the public knowledge and attitudes towards utility-scale solar projects.

Project: Micro Urban Solar Integrated Concentrators (MUSIC)
Summary/Information: The Micro Urban Solar Integrated Concentrators (MUSIC) project takes a completely new approach to collecting solar energy. It is developing innovative, thin and lightweight concentrating solar collector platforms (which ‘collect and concentrate’ the energy from sunlight) that deliver up to 400 degrees Celsius thermal energy and electricity from building roofs.

Project: New Photocathodes for Solar Hydrogen Production
Summary/Information: The goal of this New Photocathodes for Solar Hydrogen Production project is to develop an inexpensive, conceptually new system for the conversion of solar energy into hydrogen.
Lead organisation: Ian Wark Research Institute, University of South Australia

Project: Development of Commercially Viable High Efficiency Solar Cells and Module
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop commercially viable high efficiency solar cells and modules.

Project: Model Predictive Control of Thermal Components
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to develop a methodology of model predictive control to produce more reliable and better performing concentrating solar thermal systems.

Project: Australian Centre for Advanced Photovoltaics (ACAP)
Summary/Information: The Australian Centre for Advanced Photovoltaics (ACAP) project is providing a pipeline to ‘over the horizon’ photovoltaic technology, as well as training the next generation of research scientists and engineers through exposure to world-class facilities across Australia and the world.

Project: Photothermal Deflection Spectroscopy
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a fully automated turnkey solution for photothermal deflection spectroscopy.

Project: Advanced Biomass Gasification Technology
Summary/Information: The Advanced Biomass Gasification Technology project constructed and demonstrated an innovative biomass gasification technology that converts biomass, such as agricultural waste and mallee crops, into a clean gaseous fuel that can be used to generate electricity.

Project: Forecasting Distributed Solar Energy Production
Summary/Information: This project is conducting real-time analysis of some of the 650,000 residential solar photovoltaic (PV) systems widely distributed throughout Australia.

Project: Machine-Learning-Based Forecasting of Distributed Solar Energy Production
Summary/Information: The Australian National University (ANU) lead a project to develop techniques for forecasting the generation of electricity from distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, like those installed on household rooftops, with the objective of developing a commercial product that can be sold to utilities and other companies to accurately predict the output of of PV systems and therefore demand on the grid for improved efficiency and stability.

Project: Improved Measurement of Contaminants in Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Improved Measurement of Contaminants in Silicon Solar Cells project aims to compare, understand and further develop techniques that accurately identify the type and amount of efficiency-reducing contaminants in silicon solar cells. It will also investigate the lifetime effects of contamination in order to minimise its impact.

Project: High Efficiency Very Low Thermal Budget Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high efficiency, very low thermal, budget silicon solar cells through laser processing.

Project: Development of Combined Cycle Using Solar Reformed Gas
Summary/Information: This Development of Combined Cycle Using Solar Reformed Gas project aimed to demonstrate the technical and economic feasibility of a combined cycle power plant fuelled with natural gas that has been ‘upgraded’ using solar thermal energy.

Project: Copper-Zinc-Tin-Sulphide on Silicon Multi-Junction Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Copper-Zinc-Tin-Sulphide on Silicon Multi-Junction Solar Cells project aims to develop a new generation of silicon wafer solar cell technology by producing tandem devices that can improve on the world record 25% efficiency achieved by UNSW with silicon wafer-based solar cells in 2008.

Project: Plug and Play Solar Power
Summary/Information: The Plug and Play Solar Power project addressed barriers to solar hybrid power system growth by developing ‘Plug and Play’ technology.

Project: Oxide Semiconductors for Solar Energy Conversion
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate high performance titanium-oxide based semiconductors for conversion of solar energy into chemical energy required for water oxidation.

Project: Dynamic PCM Systems for High Temperature Thermal Storage
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to investigate phase change material in dynamic storage systems for high temperature thermal storage.

Project: Harnessing Energy Losses in Organic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate energy losses at the donor-acceptor interface in organic solar cells.

Project: High Efficiency Mono-Crystalline Thin-Si Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high efficiency mono-crystalline thin-silicon solar cells.

Project: Metal-Assisted Chemical Etching of Sliver Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high efficiency mono-crystalline thin-silicon solar cells.

Project: Improving the Accessibility of the System Advisor Model
Summary/Information: This project developed the necessary tools and additions to allow the System Advisor Model (SAM) to provide the same level of benefit for application to Australian geographical and market conditions as it does to the US.

Project: Pilot-Scale Plant for the Production of Solar Anti-Reflection Coatings
Summary/Information: This project involved the construction and operation of a pilot-scale manufacturing facility for an innovative anti-reflection (AR) coating that can be used on solar panels.

Project: Power Loss Analysis via Photoluminescence Imaging
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to analyse power loss via photoluminescence imaging on silicon solar cells.

Project: High Efficiency Interdigitated Back-Contact Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high efficiency interdigitated back-contact silicon solar cells with advanced fabrication techniques and simplified processes.

Project: Negatively-Charged Dielectric Films for Surface Passivation
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to further investigate the application of negatively-charged dielectric films for surface passivation of silicon solar cells.

Project: Fabrication of a New Cost Effective High Efficiency Solar Cell Structure
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a new cost effective high efficiency solar cell structure.

Project: Modelling and Applications of Advanced Thermal Storage Materials
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to model and apply advanced thermal storage materials.

Project: Role of Spin in Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate the role of spin in triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion.

Project: Fast Response Dispatchable Thermal Storage for High Temperature CSP
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate the role of spin in triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion.

Project: High-Efficiency Interdigitated Back-Contact Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high-efficiency interdigitated back-contact silicon solar cells with advanced fabrication techniques and simplified processes.

Project: Model for Community-Owned Solar
Summary/Information: The Model for Community-Owned Solar project aimed to increase the uptake of community-owned solar (COS), and resulted in a win-win situation for the City of Campbelltown and COS investors.
Lead organisation: City of Campbelltown and Local Government Association of South Australia

Project: Light Trapping for Tandem Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop industry compatible procedures for increasing light absorption in III-V/silicon tandem solar cells.

Project: Highly Efficient and Stable Photoluminescent Nanocrystal Ink
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a highly efficient and stable photoluminescent ink for improved spectral response in photovoltaic cells.

Project: Energy Yield of Photovoltaic Power Systems
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to improve translation models for predicting the energy yield of PV power systems.

Project: Wizard Power Big Dish Upgrade
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to investigate international best practice for integration with Wizard Power’s Big Dish.

Project: Improving Translation Models for Predicting Energy Yields
Summary/Information: To reduce the investment risk for large-scale photovoltaic power plants, CSIRO and its partners investigated the relationship between the manufacturer’s power rating for solar panels and the energy the panels generate over time.
Project partners: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre and Lend Lease

Project: Integrated Solar Radiation Data Sources over Australia
Summary/Information: CSIRO and its partners developed Australia’s first comprehensive solar radiation data set to help the solar energy industry measure and characertise the expected output of large scale solar power plants.
Project partners: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) and the Bureau of Meteorology (BoM)

Project: Climate-Based PV Performance and Reliability
Summary/Information: This project will provide a publicly available, high quality PV performance database containing location-specific technical, operational and performance data.
Lead organisation: Australian Photovoltaic Institute (APVI) (participants University of NSW, CAT Projects and Murdoch University)

Project: Distributed Energy Market
Summary/Information: The Distributed Energy Market project assessed a range of ways in which customers and electricity utilities might participate in a distributed energy market.

Project: Reservoir Quality in Sedimentary Geothermal Resources
Summary/Information: The Reservoir Quality in Sedimentary Geothermal Resources project analysed the only two geothermal wells drilled in Hot Sedimentary Aquifer reservoirs in Australia to evaluate why the flow of fluid was significantly less than expected.
Lead organisation: South Australian Centre for Geothermal Energy Research (SACGER) and the University of Adelaide
Project partners: CSIRO, South Australian Department of State Development (formerly DMITRE), Geodynamics Ltd, Raya Group Ltd (Formerly Panax Geothermal Ltd), South Australian Museum

Project: Development of an Australian Solar Map
Summary/Information: This project involves the development of an interactive live solar photovoltaic (PV) map that tracks the uptake and impact of PV across Australia.
Lead organisation: Australian Photovoltaic Institute (participants University of NSW, CAT Projects, Sunwiz, SMA)

Project: Solar Resource Mapping Project
Summary/Information: The Solar Resource Mapping Project contributed to the creation of the Australian Solar Energy Information System, funded the development of better satellite models for depicting solar radiation, and funded eight additional solar radiation ground monitoring stations.

Project: Cost Effective Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop cost effective silicon solar cells using upgraded-metallurgical-grade silicon.

Project: Colloidal Nanoparticle Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop high efficiency hetrojunction solar cells based on colloidal nanoparticles suitable for application to a variety of device geometries.

Project: Plasmonic Rear Reflectors for Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate and develop increased rear surface reflectance in silicon solar cells using plasmonic.

Project: Hybrid Concentrating Solar Thermal Systems
Summary/Information: The Hybrid Concentrating Solar Thermal Systems project demonstrated the successful design, integration and operation of a high temperature solar heat (150 to 200 degrees Celsius) building space heating and cooling system, and provided a pathway for realising a world first high efficiency solar thermal desiccant air conditioning system.

Project: Solar Hybrid Fuels
Summary/Information: The Solar Hybrid Fuels project looked at two streams of work. The first stream aimed to make synthetic gas (syngas) from natural gas at lower temperatures compatible with conventional solar thermal storage while maintaining high efficiency, to allow for the 24/7 operation of an industrial solar fuels plant. The second stream of work produced a detailed roadmap and recommendations for solar hybrid fuel technology options and opportunities suitable for Australia.

Project: Solar Energy Management System for Utilities
Summary/Information: CSIRO developed a world-first ‘firm’ solar energy system to reliably reduce the impacts of peak demand by tackling air conditioner electrical consumption, which is the primary cause of peak demand in Australian electricity networks.

Project: BPS bioWAVE Ocean Pilot at Port Fairy
Summary/Information: This project aimed to demonstrate an innovative new method for converting wave energy into electricity using the patented bioWAVE technology to efficiently convert wave energy to mechanical energy via a unique mechanical-to-electrical energy converter.

Project: Potential Network Benefits of CST Power
Summary/Information: This study was undertaken to quantify the potential benefits of installing CSP generation at constrained network locations in the National Electricity Market (NEM).

Project: Integrated PV Solar Roofing
Summary/Information: This project aimed to develop low cost building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) roofing for mass market residential and commercial applications on Australian buildings.

Project: Generating Renewable Energy from Almond Waste
Summary/Information: The Generating Renewable Energy from Almond Waste project analysed the commercial viability of generating renewable energy from almond waste.

Project: Oceanlinx 1MW Commercial Wave Energy Demonstrator
Summary/Information: (Project closed 20 June 2014) The Oceanlinx commercial wave energy demonstrator is a 3,000 tonne structure measuring approximately 21 metres wide by 24 metres long. The device was designed to sit in shallow water, using oscillating water column (OWC) technology to generate 1MW peak output.
Project partners: OEC Pty Ltd, Strategic formwork, Techport, COOE Pty Ltd, ACOR, ABB, VACON, Power & Drive Solutions, Broens Ltd

Project: Plasmonic Light Trapping for Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate plasmonic light trapping for solar cells.

Project: Effect of Nano-Size Structures & Composition on Solar Water Disinfection
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to assess the effect of titanium dioxide based nanostructures and semiconducting properties on oxidation of solar water.

Project: Hybridisation of Concentrated Solar Thermal
Summary/Information: The Hybridisation of Concentrated Solar Thermal project achieved the world’s first practical demonstration of pilot scale Post-Combustion Carbon dioxide capture (PCC) process integrated with solar thermal energy and demonstrates an important low emissions energy solution to achieving substantial emissions reductions from Australian coal fired electricity generation with the potential for large scale deployment of solar thermal fields in Australia.

Project: Least-Cost Carbon Abatement Modelling
Summary/Information: This project is developing a software tool that links together weather variability, renewable and fossil technologies, transmission and economic market models, in many hundreds of thousands of combinations, to find the most affordable ways to significantly increase the use of renewable energy in the electricity system.
Project partners: University of NSW, Australian Energy market Operator, Bureau of Meteorology, GE and Market Reform

Project: Achieving Cost-Affective Abatement
Summary/Information: Prior to these studies being undertaken, there was limited evidence and supporting information as to the relative benefits of a Renewable Energy Target versus a carbon price in terms of the transition to a low carbon energy system.

Project: Daly River Solar Research Project
Summary/Information: PWC owns and operates over 50 mini-grids across the Northern Territory, providing power to remote Indigenous communities. These mini-grids predominantly rely on diesel fuel for power generation, which is associated with high operational costs, significant risk exposure to future price increases and greenhouse gas emissions. PWC recognises the opportunity provided by solar technologies to reduce its reliance on diesel fuel for remote power generation.

Project: High Efficiency, Multi-Junction CPV Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The High Efficiency, Multi-Junction CPV Solar Cells project is developing virtual germanium (Ge) and germanium-tin (Ge-Sn) on silicon wafers for the next generation of multiple-junction solar cells, which are low in cost but highly efficient, meaning they can convert more energy from sunlight than most other solar cells.

Project: Next Generation Crystalline Silicon on Glass Modules
Summary/Information: This project aimed to increase the efficiency of crystalline silicon on glass thin-film solar cells beyond the current world record and to reduce the manufacturing costs by developing new breakthrough approaches to the cell fabrication.

Project: Central Receiver CPV Pilot Project Stage 2
Summary/Information: This project demonstrated the world’s first pre-commercial pilot of a central receiver system that uses solar photovoltaic (PV) energy conversion.

Project: Improved High-Temperature Receivers for Dish Concentrators
Summary/Information: This project is investigating heat loss from high-temperature solar thermal receivers and developing the next generation of improved receiver designs to reduce that loss.

Project: Pilot Study on Load Control and Optimisation
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of hybrid technologies to develop an AI smart grid control and optimisation system.

Project: Perth Wave Energy Project
Summary/Information: The Perth Wave Energy Project is the world’s first commercial-scale wave energy array that is connected to the grid and has the ability to produce desalinated water.

Project: Small Scale Hydropower Technologies Impact on Australian Native Fish
Summary/Information: This Small Scale Hydropower Technologies Impact on Australian Native Fish project produced detailed scientific information on the effects small hydro has on native fish species, which could be used to improve the design and operation of small hydro systems.
Project partners: Office of Environment and Heritage (NSW), NSW Department of Primary Industries, Aquatic Ecosystems (NSW), UNSW Manly Hydraulics Lab

Project: Cost Effective Industrial Scale Synthesis
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a cost effective industrial scale synthesis of regio regular poly-3-hexylthiophene using flow chemistry.

Project: Development of Hybrid Solar Thermal Reactors for Materials Processing
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to optimise the use of solar thermal energy in the design and construction of a hybrid solar/electric reactor for high temperature processes by utilising a novel solar simulator design.

Project: Semiconductor Nanowire Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop III-V compound semiconductor nanowire solar cells.

Project: Australian Feedstock and Refining Capacity
Summary/Information: Qantas and Shell Australia collaborated to undertake a feasibility study into Australian feedstock (material that can be processed into biofuel) and refining capacity to produce Sustainable Aviation Fuel.

Project: Enhancing Efficiencies in Printed Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This Enhancing Efficiencies in Printed Solar Cells project successfully improved the production of effective and reliable, low-cost printed organic solar cells by controlling the way the organic components in the cell align with each other at a microscopic (molecular) level during the ink drying process.

Project: Analysis of Variations in Instantaneous Weather Effects
Summary/Information: This project has developed innovative strategies for the distribution of mature, commercialised PV technologies within existing electricity networks, and in particular identified that up to 10MW of distributed solar PV could be installed within the Alice Springs grid.
Lead organisation: Ekistica Pty Ltd trading as CAT Projects

Project: Local Doping Using Laser Chemical Processing Technology
Summary/Information: The Local Doping Using Laser Chemical Processing Technology project further developed a novel doping method called Laser Chemical Processing (LCP) so it can be used in the production of high efficiency, low cost cells.

Project: Solar Efficiency Optimisation of Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to improve solar efficiency of hybrid organic-inorganic solar cells.

Project: Development of High Temperature Phase Change Storage Systems
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to develop high temperature phase change storage systems and a test facility.

Project: Optimising Building Integrated Photovoltaic Thermal for Retrofitting
Summary/Information: The project objective was to broaden the value proposition of Building Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) systems through an enhanced understanding of the performance and optimal design of BIPV systems with added thermal functionality, i.e. Building Integrated Photovoltaic Thermal (BIPVT) systems.

Project: Demonstrate Higher Efficiency Third Generation Photovoltaics
Summary/Information: The Demonstrate Higher Efficiency Third Generation Photovoltaics project aims to increase the efficiency of one type of third generation solar cell by increasing the number of layers of nanoscopic silicon crystals (silicon nanocrystals or Si NC) in silicon oxide and silicon nitride.

Project: Time & Spectrally Resolved Photo-Silicon Solar Cell Characterisation
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop a new time decay luminescence measurement technique for silicon solar cell characterisation.

Project: ITO Free Efficient Organic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop indium-tin-oxide (ITO) free, efficient organic solar cells based on textured graphene electrodes

Project: Data Fusion and Machine Learning
Summary/Information: The resulting information and software can be used to improve exploration, discovery and characterisation methods for targeted geothermal exploration.

Project: Solar Supercritical Organic Rankine Cycle
Summary/Information: The Solar Supercritical Organic Rankine Cycle project demonstrates an innovative CST system’s ability to provide 24/7 electricity. The project will use integrated solar thermal storage while operating as an automated plant with a gas heater.

Project: Large-Area Amorphous Silicon Ultrathin Film Plasmonic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to achieve more cost-effective, large-area amorphous silicon ultrathin film plasmonic solar cells, which can be scaled up towards industrial application.

Project: Solar Gasification Using Renewable Energy
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to assess the technical and economic viability of production of liquid transport fuel via solar gasification of low-grade carbonaceous fuels.

Project: Solution Deposited Thin-Film Tandem Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop solution deposited thin-film tandem solar cells.

Project: High-Energy Algal Fuels
Summary/Information: The High-Energy Algal Fuels project integrated macroalgal biomass production into existing industrial infrastructure for the bioremediation of toxins from wastewater and the reduction of carbon emissions through photosynthesis. The biomass did not compete for arable land or quality water by being cultivated in waste water.

Project: Thermionic Emissions from MAX Phase Materials
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to develop thermionic cathode materials based on MAX phases.

Project: Spectral Beam Splitting for Improving Energy Conversion Efficiency
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to examine spectral beam splitting systems to improve the energy conversion efficiency in hybrid concentrating solar collectors.

Project: Validation of CST Solar Array Performance Modelling
Summary/Information: Building on an existing testing and demonstration facility comprising 200 mirrors, Vast Solar constructed and deployed an additional 500 mirrors, developed a higher temperature receiver, operated the facility and gathered performance data, then determined operational requirements.

Project: Understanding and Optimising Dielectric Charge in Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to understand and optimise dielectric charge in industry applicable solar cells.

Project: Facilitating High Penetration PV Integration into the Electricity Network
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to facilitate high penetration photovoltaic (PV) integration into the electricity network.

Project: Material Characteristics of Crystalline Si Thin-Film Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to study the impacts of material characteristics on the performance of crystalline silicon thin-film solar cells.

Project: Light-Weight and Flexible Solid-State Dye-Sensitised Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate light-weight and flexible solid-state dye-sensitised solar cells.

Project: Testing Facility for Storing Heat from Solar Energy
Summary/Information: This project established a world class facility to test newly-developed high temperature storage systems and technologies operating at up to 900 degrees Celcius.

Project: Trapping Detrapping and Loss Mechanisms in Dye Sensitised Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate trapping, detrapping and loss mechanisms in dye sensitised solar cells.

Project: Nanostructured and Metamaterial Photovoltaics
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop novel simulation methods for greater insights into nanostructured and metamaterial photovoltaics.
