Project: Development of a State of the Art Solid Particle Receiver CST System
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to design and assess the commercialisation potential of a concentrated solar thermal tower system, based on a high temperature solid particle receiver.

Project: Better Modelling of Concentrated Solar Thermal Power Plants
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar thermal technologies to investigate better modelling of concentrated solar thermal power plants.

Project: Towards a Practical Hot Carrier Solar Cell
Summary/Information: This project is investigating suitable materials and structures that could be used to produce a working model of a Hot Carrier solar cell, which can more effectively harvest energy from sunlight.
Project partners: Arizona State University, Purdue University, National Renewable Energy Laboratory, and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory

Project: Cost Effective Gallium Arsenide Phosphide Top Solar Cell
Summary/Information: The project aims to cut solar energy costs by developing a high voltage solar cell that will be 40% more efficient than solar cells being used today.

Project: Multi-Junction Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project aims to produce the first silicon-based solar cell with more than 30% efficiency, challenging the UNSW-held world record for conventional silicon wafer technology.

Project: Solar-Driven Supercritical CO2 Brayton Cycle
Summary/Information: Building on CSIRO’s solar air turbine technology, this project examined ways to reduce the cost of solar energy to less than 10 cents per kilowatt hour (c/kWh) which would make solar energy cost competitive with existing power stations.

Project: Optimisation of Central Receivers for Advanced Power Cycles
Summary/Information: The Optimisation of Central Receivers for Advanced Power Cycles examines if concentrating solar power (CSP) technology is to be widely adopted for electricity production its costs must be substantially reduced, similar to the cost reduction achieved by solar photovoltaic technology in recent years.

Project: Roof-Mounted Hybrid CST System
Summary/Information: This project aims to develop and commercialise a roof-mounted hybrid solar concentrator PV/thermal system that cost effectively delivers solar heating, cooling and electricity.

Project: Future fuels
Thermoelectric Generator for Concentrated Solar Thermal Systems
Summary/Information: The Thermoelectric Generator for Concentrated Solar Thermal Systems project developed and applied high-performance thermoelectric materials and technologies to concentrated solar thermal (CST) systems.

Project: Characterising and Forecasting Grid Connected Solar Energy
Summary/Information: The project looked at new techniques of applying known models to the forecasting challenge, and ways to understand how solar and wind can smoothly integrate into the electricity grid.
Project partners: University of South Australia, Australian Photovoltaic Association, Epuron and Australian Bureau of Meteorology

Project: Industry Ready N-Type Silicon Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The Industry Ready N-Type Silicon Solar Cells project successfully increased the amount of energy a solar cell can convert from sunlight without extra manufacturing costs per cell by combining the existing fast and inexpensive methods used to make today’s standard silicon solar cells with the latest advances in high efficiency silicon solar cells.
Project partners: Trina Solar and University of NSW

Project: Printing Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project developed new materials and solar cell designs with enhanced performance that significantly improve the efficiency and durability of organic photovoltaic (OPV) solar cells.

Project: Synthesis of Organic Photovoltaic Materials using Continuous Flow Methods
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop continuous flow methodologies for synthesis of organic photovoltaic materials.

Project: Analysis of Potential for Liquid Metal Heat Transfer
Summary/Information: This project demonstrated the world’s first pre-commercial pilot of enabling technologies to analyse the potential for liquid metal heat transfer fluids to improve the commercial competitiveness and dispatchability of concentrating solar power.

Project: Pilot of Rooftop CST and CPV-T Solar Energy Systems
Summary/Information: (Project closed 7 November 2014) Chromasun was partnering with the Futuris Group of Companies to develop and establish an Australian pilot manufacturing capability for the Chromasun Micro-Concentrator (MCT) concentrating solar thermal (CST) product. ARENA’s funding commitment was $3.4 million.

Project: Kogan Creek Solar Boost Project
Summary/Information: The Kogan Creek Solar Boost Project set out to install a 44 megawatts of concentrating solar power (CSP) at CS Energy’s 750 megawatt coal-fired Kogan Creek Power Station.

Project: Improved PV Energy Conversion
Summary/Information: This project aimed to overcome the limitations of normal solar cells by developing a solar cell coating that can harvest sub-threshold light.

Project: Thin Film Solar Cell: A Novel Alternative for TW-level Thin Film PV
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to design and manufacture high quality copper-zinc-tin-sulfur (CZTS) thin film solar cells for TW-level thin film PV.

Project: Development of Novel Water-Based Materials for Commercial Organic Photovoltaics
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop novel water-based materials for commercial organic photovoltaics.

Project: Development and Characterisation of Ion Implantation for all Back Contact Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to develop and characterise ion implantation for all back contact solar cells.

Project: Intermediate Layers for Laser Crystallised Silicon Thin Film Solar Cells on Glass
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of solar photovoltaic (PV) technologies to investigate intermediate layers for laser crystallised silicon thin film solar cells on glass.

Project: Tandem Quantum Dot Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project is demonstrating a new type of photovoltaic solar cell that combines the reliability of silicon with a technology that can more effectively collect visible and invisible solar energy (called a tandem solar cell) thereby creating a new type of tandem solar cell based solely on silicon.

Project: Power Cube Power Tower Receiver
Summary/Information: This project is aims to reduce the cost of utility scale photovoltaics by developing a technology that splits sunlight into specific wavelength bands and converts each into electricity using commercially available solar cells.

Project: The Hot Carrier Solar Cell
Summary/Information: The aim of this project was to develop a prototype Hot Carrier (HC) solar cell and establish routes toward the development of practical devices. The HC solar cell is a promising advanced photovoltaics or so called “third generation” concept which aims to tackle the major efficiency loss in conventional solar cells.
Project partners: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (USA) National Renewable Energy Laboratory (USA) Purdue University (USA) Arizona State University (USA)

Project: Thermal Energy Storage Systems with High Temperature Phase Change Material
Summary/Information: This project is a study of research and development of enabling technologies to investigate high performance thermal energy storage systems with high temperature phase change material.

Project: Solar Air Turbine Systems
Summary/Information: The Solar Air Turbine Systems project involved CSIRO and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries developing and testing the components of the world’s most powerful solar air turbines to increase its efficiency while decreasing its manufacturing, installation and operation costs.

Project: Geoscience Australia Solar Research Data
Summary/Information: A study of enabling technologies to identify solar irradiance across Australia.

Project: Advanced Solar Thermal Energy Storage Technologies
Summary/Information: This project involved CSIRO working with Spanish company Abengoa to find cost-effective ways to collect and store heat from sunlight (solar thermal energy) in order to increase user confidence in solar energy, minimise disruption to the electricity grid and make it more economic for solar power plants to produce electricity.

Project: Advanced Steam-Generating Receivers
Summary/Information: The Advanced Steam-Generating Receivers project successfully demonstrated that significant reductions in the Levelised Cost of Electricity can be achieved by moving operation of concentrating solar thermal plants to higher temperatures and pressures. Additionally, the project has shown that using once through boiler designs is a suitable in concentrating solar thermal receivers.

Project: Next Generation SLIVER Cells
Summary/Information: This report details the Next generation SLIVER cells project aimed to maximise the likelihood of successful commercialisation of SLIVER technology.

Project: Plasmonics for High Efficiency Solar Cells
Summary/Information: The project aimed to commercialise a new way of increasing light absorption in solar cells using a technology called ‘plasmonics’.
Project partners: University of NSW, IMEC (Belgium), Imperial College (UK), Chalmers University (Sweden), Photovoltech (Belgium), QantaSol (UK)

Project: Cooper Basin Enhanced Geothermal Systems
Summary/Information: (The Cooper Basin Enhanced Geothermal Systems project closed 10 December 2015). While conventional geothermal power generation uses volcanic geology, Geodynamics is leading the development of a new technology called Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS).

Project: High Efficiency Silicon Solar Cell Technology
Summary/Information: The High Efficiency Silicon Solar Cell Technology project is the first to implement laboratory-proven advanced cell process technology at the Solar Industrial Research Facility (SIRF) at UNSW.

Project: Overcoming Performance Limitations of Commercial Solar Cells
Summary/Information: This project aimed to improve solar cell performance and reduce production costs by mass-producing solar cells using large-scale commercial manufacturing. It achieved the world’s first 20% efficient p-type CZ cell fabricated using commercial equipment, 10 years ahead of the timing predicted by international experts.

Project: New Materials and Architectures for Organic Solar Cells
Summary/Information: Organic solar cells are widely viewed as having significant potential for delivering low cost solar photovoltaic (PV) power, but currently are not as efficient as other low cost alternatives in converting sunlight to energy.

Project: Inline Inspection Tools for Photovoltaic Manufacturing
Summary/Information: This project developed two inline inspection tools, which are integrated into solar cell manufacturing ‘lines’ to help solar research organisations reduce the cost of manufacturing photovoltaic cells.
Project partners: Australian National University, Applied Materials (China) and Suntech R&D

Project: Fabrication of Thermionic Device using Advanced Ceramics
Summary/Information: This project created a working prototype of a device called a thermionic energy converter, which directly converts the heat generated by concentrated sunlight into electricity.

Project: King Island Renewable Energy Integration Project
Summary/Information: This project demonstrates a world-leading power system that combines several renewable energy technologies, smart tech integrations and energy management technologies. The system will supply over 65% of King Island’s annual energy needs using renewable energy, reducing CO2 emissions by more than 95%.

Project: Cane2Fuel: Feasibility of Producing Biofuel from Sugarcane Waste
Summary/Information: The Cane2Fuel: Feasibility of Producing Biofuel from Sugarcane Waste project used an integrated approach to investigate the technical and commercial feasibility of producing biofuel from sugarcane bagasse, which is a by-product of the sugar production process.

Project: Demonstrate Commercial Production of Bio-Crude Oil from Biomass
Summary/Information: The project involved the design, construction and successful operation of a commercial demonstration facility for the conversion of inedible plant material (biomass) into a bio-crude oil with similar characteristics to traditional fossil crude.
Project partners: University of Sydney and Ignite Energy Resources Ltd

Project: Generation 2 Ethanol from Sugarcane Waste
Summary/Information: Using specialised yeast bred for the purpose and an advanced refinery process called Fuel AND Food, the project converted sugarcane waste into three products: ethanol fuel, high nutrition animal feed and an environmentally friendly potential substitute for coal.

Project: Sustainable Production of Transport Biofuels
Summary/Information: The cost-effective conversion of farm-grown mallee crops into liquid fuels could help to significantly reduce carbon dioxide emissions from the transport industry, promote regional economic development and help control dryland salinity.
Project partners: CSIRO Sustainable Ecosystems and WA Department of Environment and Conservation

Project: Production of Biofuel from Microalgae
Summary/Information: This project developed a technology that produces biodiesel and other valuable by-products from microalgal biomass harvested from large-scale algal farms. Microalgae are microscopic plant-like organisms that directly convert carbon dioxide and sunlight into biochemical energy.

Project: Solar Thermal Research Hub
Summary/Information: The Solar Thermal Research Hub project involved CSIRO constructing Australia’s largest solar thermal research hub at the CSIRO National Solar Energy Centre in Newcastle.

Project: Geothermal Heat Exchanger in Hot Sedimentary Rocks
Summary/Information: This project initially aimed to drill two geothermal wells, fracture the ground and complete test flows.
Lead organisation: MNGI PTY LTD (Trading Name: Petratherm Limited)
